kit-suiza.titulo: Swiss Kit: the official 7-day reserve (9 liters of water per person)
kit-suiza.resumen: The list the Swiss State recommends keeping at home, translated and bought in Spain: 9 liters of water per person, a week's food, radio, portable stove, masks and cash. From 120 €.
kit-suiza.coste_total: 120-260 € per person for 7 days (less if you rotate what you already eat)
kit-suiza.paraQuien: For those who want a domestic reserve with numbers, not good intentions: the official Swiss list translated for a Spanish apartment, with quantities, prices and what to rotate every six months.
kit-suiza.paraQuien_no: It is not an evacuation kit or a backpack kit: it is a reserve to stay at home. If your plan is to leave the city with just what you're wearing, you need the evacuation kit. And it does not replace medication or the family plan.
kit-suiza.busc: emergency reserve kit 7 days water food portable stove

antes: Count the water using the Swiss rule: 9 liters per person, and add your pet and the heat in your area
Rotate the food: the reserve is normal food you eat and replace, not a separate cupboard that expires
Check the date on each water container and write it on the cap; bottled water expires too
Store chronic medication with the prescription in a cool place: it is the point no generic kit covers
Keep the cash in small notes and separate from your everyday wallet
Test the portable stove and radio once a year, with new batteries
durante: Drink before you are thirsty: water is the first supply to fail and the hardest to improvise
Listen to the official radio twice a day; it is the channel that stays alive when the mobile network goes down
Cook during the day and with ventilation: a gas stove indoors kills with carbon monoxide if there is no air
Ration masks and disinfectant if you have to go out or clean contaminated areas
Do not open the fridge unless necessary: every opening loses hours of cold
despues: Replace what you use within the same week, not 'someday': a half-done reserve is not a reserve
Check dates and note what expired unused (usually it is what you don't like eating)
Wash the stove, dry the batteries and put everything back where you first found it

secciones.titulo: Water: 9 liters per person that do not depend on the tap
secciones.intro: It is the most concrete figure in the entire Swiss list and the one that most people fail to meet without knowing it. Nine litres is a pack of six 1.5 L bottles: drinking and cooking for a few days, not counting hygiene.

items.descripcion: The practical way to store 16 litres without taking over the kitchen. They stack, rotate and do not depend on the tap.

items.producto: Bottled water to rotate every 6 months
items.descripcion: A daily-use reserve that is consumed and replenished: that way the water never expires in the cupboard.
Turns questionable water into drinkable water. It is what separates 9 litres from a whole week when the supply comes back cloudy.

secciones.intro: Switzerland asks for one week of normal food: rice, pasta, oil, canned food, UHT milk, dried fruit, chocolate. No special rations; food you already eat, so it can be rotated.

items.descripcion: The base that can be eaten without cooking or refrigeration. Alternate fish, legumes and vegetables so you do not always eat the same thing.
It lasts for years, fills you up and only needs water and heat. With the camping stove it cooks just like at home.

items.producto: Pasta, rice and legumes in packets
items.descripcion: A pantry assortment to complete the week without depending on the fridge.
The detail that ruins a perfect pantry: without a can opener, the cans do not open.

secciones.intro: Switzerland says it explicitly: gas stove. Storing food and having nothing to heat it with is the most common mistake in household reserves.

items.descripcion: Hot coffee, rice and canned food without power. With spare canisters and always used in a ventilated area.
If you have the space, a domestic heater gives you weeks of autonomy with one cylinder. Never inside a closed bedroom.
The lighter runs out and will not light upside down. Long matches reach the burner without burning yourself.

secciones.intro: When the mobile network goes down, the radio keeps broadcasting. That is why it is on the Swiss list alongside spare batteries, and not the mobile phone.

items.descripcion: The information channel that survives a blackout. Tune in to the useful stations beforehand and write down the frequency.
Move around the house without draining your phone battery, which is what you need to make calls.
Hands-free for cooking, fixing things or going down to the garage. During a blackout, this makes the difference.

secciones.titulo: Hygiene and health: the 50 masks and medication
secciones.intro: The most surprising Swiss figure: 50 masks per person. It was added after the pandemic because a health crisis also leaves people without supplies. At home, 20 FFP2 masks cover the domestic scenario.

items.descripcion: For going out, cleaning contaminated areas or living with a sick person without a healthcare system.
Cuts, stove burns and bumps are the real emergencies in a blackout, not movie-style catastrophes.
Rationed water means less cleaning: disinfectant makes up for it.

items.producto: Chronic medication: one week of your treatment
items.descripcion: The most personal item on the list and the only one you can't buy in a pack. With a prescription, in a cool place and with the expiry date in sight.

secciones.titulo: What Switzerland lists and almost nobody copies
secciones.intro: Cash, batteries and pet food. These are three lines from the Swiss leaflet that appear on almost no Spanish list and that make a difference on day one of a real blackout.

items.descripcion: Keeps your phone alive for a whole day and charges the radio if it's rechargeable. Charge it the same day you check your reserves.
If you have a dog or cat, their week of food counts just as much as yours. Almost nobody includes it.
When card readers and ATMs don't respond, cash still buys. Sixty euros in 10 and 20 euro notes.

kit-basico-72h.resumen: EU resilience backpack: 21 verified items, checklist with tick boxes, one-click Amazon basket. Updated 2026 guide.
kit-basico-72h.coste_total: 180-300 € (two-person household; first-aid kit and tools are household items, not per person)
kit-basico-72h.paraQuien: For any household in Spain, wherever you start. It is the resilience bag the EU has called for since March 2025 — water, food, light, information, documents and shelter to last 72 hours without services — with every product checked: no listings that say one thing and sell another. If you are only going to put together one kit, make it this one.
kit-basico-72h.paraQuien_no: It's not a backpack for walking out, and it doesn't replace the specific kit for your hazard (DANA, mountains, car). If you live in a flood-prone area or with dependent people, complete it with the evacuation kit and the baby kit or the elderly person's kit.

antes: Put the kit together with the whole family and keep it in a known, accessible place
Check expiry dates (water, food, batteries, medication) every 6 months
Write emergency numbers on paper: 112, your local Protección Civil

Turn on mobile alerts in your phone settings: the ES-Alert system (National Alert Network) sends warnings directly to people in the affected area. The Basic Guidelines approved in April 2026 incorporate it into all civil protection plans
durante: Follow only instructions from official sources (112, Protección Civil)
Ration water and phone battery
Keep the battery-powered radio on in the FM band
despues: Replace what you've used as soon as possible
Note down what was missing and adjust the kit

errores: Buying without checking the actual product page: half of the online 'essentials' lists link to a women's raincoat, a decorative poster instead of a map, or tablets for 200-litre tanks. Before you pay, check that the photo, gender/size and dosage unit are the ones you need.
Buying only bottled water and having no plan B: if it runs out, purification tablets for 10 € give you treated tap or rainwater.
Storing everything in the storage room or the top cupboard. In a blackout with no light you need to find it in 30 seconds, better next to the door.
Not writing the purchase date on each pack: after two years you won't know what's old and you'll throw away half your supplies.
Forgetting the radio. In a long crisis your phone goes silent; the battery-powered radio is your only link to what Protección Civil orders.
Buying everything all at once and then letting it sit. It works better to add two or three items each week with your shopping.

secciones.intro: The first thing to run out and the only thing you can't improvise. 3 litres per person per day for drinking, a reserve with a tap, and a system to make questionable water safe to drink when it runs out.

items.producto: Mineral water in 1.5 L bottles (pack of 6 = 9 L)
items.descripcion: Nine litres bottled: the 3 L/day one person needs for three days. Rotate every six months and use it in the kitchen.
Eight litres with a built-in tap: dispense without opening anything and it stands upright in the pantry. The household's base reserve.

items.producto: Aquatabs water purification tablets (50 units, 1 L/unit)
items.descripcion: One tablet per litre: 50 litres of drinking water per box. Clear dose for a bottle, not a tank, which is what you really need.

secciones.intro: Food you can eat without cooking, water or electricity—and that you'll actually want to eat for three days straight.

items.descripcion: 515 kcal per serving, prepared with hot water in 8 minutes and eaten straight from the pouch. Years of shelf life.

items.producto: Sardines in olive oil (5 cans × 120 g)
items.descripcion: Protein and healthy fat with no fridge or cooking: open and eat. Five cans cover several lunches.
About 130 kcal per 35 g bar: a compact pocket snack, not a full meal. It adds to your supplies, it doesn't replace a meal.

secciones.intro: To see and be seen, and to keep your phone and radio alive. A headlamp leaves your hands free: it's the flashlight you'll actually use.

items.descripcion: 3 AAA batteries, 22 h on low mode and 6 h on high, red light so you don't blind anyone. Hands-free for going down stairs in the dark.

items.producto: INIU power bank 20,000 mAh (22.5 W, USB-C)
items.descripcion: Four or five phone charges, with USB-C cable included. Your phone is your map, your torch and your radio: no battery, no anything.

items.producto: AA and AAA alkaline batteries (24 + 24, 10 years)
items.descripcion: Twenty-four of each type, with a ten-year shelf life. They power the radio, the headlamp and whatever comes next.

secciones.intro: Knowing what's happening and where the rest of the family is. When the network is down, radio and paper win.

items.producto: FM/AM radio with hand crank, solar and USB (2,000 mAh)
items.descripcion: Three ways to charge it — crank, solar panel and USB — plus a torch and SOS button. If the internet and mobile network go down, it's the only channel still broadcasting.
The official map from the Ministry of Transport: roads, towns and alternative exits. Works without batteries and without signal.
Five whistles with lanyard: they carry far further than your voice and need no power. The cheapest locator in the kit.

secciones.intro: Photocopies and some cash in small bills. Five minutes of preparation that saves you months of paperwork.

items.descripcion: Watertight seal: ID card, policies, prescriptions and your phone stay dry even if the backpack ends up in a puddle.
Two flat pockets worn under your clothes: cash, cards and a spare key kept close to your body. If you lose the backpack, you don't lose your papers.

secciones.intro: What keeps a small cut from becoming a problem in a place with no running water or pharmacy.

items.producto: Complete Lewis-Plast first aid kit (309 pieces, European standard)
items.descripcion: 309 pieces compliant with the European first aid kit standard: gauze, bandages, medical tape, scissors, gloves and dressings. A real base, not a decorative case.
One and a half litres of 70% gel: hand hygiene without water for days. One in the backpack, one in the car.
Fifty CE-certified FFP2 masks: smoke, dust and unhealthy air. The European list added them after the pandemic and they still make sense.

secciones.intro: Keeping your body temperature up is what separates an uncomfortable night from a medical emergency. And wet = cold.

items.descripcion: Five large blankets that retain body heat and weigh 55 g each. One per person and two spare.

items.producto: Unisex waterproof poncho with hood (one size)
items.descripcion: Unisex ripstop poncho, 8,000 mm hydrostatic head, with hood and one size; it also works as a tarp. Covers you and your backpack.

secciones.intro: Open, cut, screw and light a fire. No batteries, no signal and no depending on anyone.

items.descripcion: Blade, saw, can opener, corkscrew and screwdrivers in 60 grams. The tool that solves what you hadn't planned for.
Four boxes of XXL matches: they light a candle or a stove without burning your fingers and cope with damp better than a lighter.

kit-dana.titulo: DANA / Flood Kit: 14 items to protect your home (2026)
kit-dana.resumen: DANA Kit: 14 items to protect your home from flooding. Guide based on official Civil Protection recommendations.
kit-dana.paraQuien: For anyone who lives or works in Levante, the Balearic Islands, the Guadalquivir area, dry riverbed zones, ravines or watercourses with housing developments nearby. DANA is the most frequent risk in Spain: water that arrives in minutes, without enough advance warning.
kit-dana.paraQuien_no: It is not suitable for the slow flooding scenario of a river in the north (there time is on your side and the priority is to shut off utilities and move things out of the house). And it does not replace the basic kit: without drinking water and food, a DANA that cuts off roads drags on.

antes: Keep the basic 72h kit within reach
Do not leave loose objects on terraces or in gardens that could be swept away
If you live in a flood-prone area, prepare sandbags and get out of the basement
With an orange or red warning, keep alerts enabled on your phone: the new Basic Flood Guideline (BOE, 27/04/2026) consolidates ES-Alert as a direct warning channel for the public

Check the warnings before it rains, not when it is already coming down: on AEMET (aemet.es, Warnings section) or Meteoalarm, the European warning service. Civil Protection considers torrential rain to be above 60 mm/hour; with an orange or red warning, the plan for the day changes: don't go out to run errands.

Move the kit, documents and charger today to a cupboard on the highest floor. On the ground floor, in the basement or garage, they get soaked just when you need them and the water won't let you go down. It's free and takes five minutes.
durante: Do not drive or walk through flooded areas: 15 cm of water can sweep a person away
Go up to upper floors if water enters the house; do not use the elevator
Switch off the electricity if there is a risk of contact with water

If water reaches you in the car, leave it and go up to a tall building: a car floats and is swept away by less than half a meter of moving water. Never cross an underpass, a ford or a dry riverbed, either by car or on foot: 15 cm of water can already sweep a person away.

Don't go down to the garage to move the car and don't go out to watch the floodwater: that's where serious DANA accidents happen. Stay on an upper floor with the radio on, and call or message anyone who lives alone nearby.
despues: Don't drink tap water until you've confirmed it's safe to drink
Don't turn on lights or devices until you've checked that the wiring is dry
Photograph the damage for your insurance before you move anything

When cleaning up mud, wear an FFP2 mask, gloves and boots: dry mud gets inhaled and it comes from sewage. Open everything wide and dry out in the first 48 hours, or mold will stay in the walls and furniture.

Before drinking or cooking with tap water, check with your local council that the supply is safe: after a flood there may be a do-not-drink notice. If in the slightest doubt, bottled water or boil it for one minute.

errores: Relying on the mobile alert and having nothing ready until it goes off. In the 2024 DANA many people had no time to spare: the kit has to be ready beforehand.
Going down to the garage or the storage room to save things once it's already raining hard. It's the classic accident.
Turning on the light or touching wet sockets: electrocution on the ground floor is one of the most common causes of death in floods.
Going back too early and walking through the mud without gloves or boots: it's full of sewage, glass and metal.

Not noting down or photographing anything: damage claims go wrong without evidence and the deadlines of the Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros keep running. Take dated photos and video from day one, including of what you throw out. And don't store the kit in the basement: the first place to flood is the worst spot for emergency supplies.

secciones.intro: If you're caught out on foot or in the car, what you decide in two minutes is worth more than anything you buy afterwards.

items.descripcion: Fitted hood and sealed seams for torrential rain.
Knee-high rubber: contaminated water, mud and sharp objects.
Protection when handling debris and working in water.

secciones.intro: In a flooded home, the biggest silent risk isn't the water: it's the electricity still in the cables.

items.descripcion: LED model with 100+ lumens. Keep spare batteries separately.
Protection against electrocution when reconnecting power in wet areas.

secciones.intro: Cheap, quick measures you put in place when an alert is issued, before the water arrives.

items.descripcion: Improvised water barriers at low doors and windows.

items.producto: Tape and plastic sheeting to seal windows
items.descripcion: Sealing windows and cracks against wind-driven rain.

secciones.intro: The days after are when injuries and illness happen: mud, damp and damaged installations.

items.descripcion: DANA floodwater leaves mud mixed with sewage: disinfect everything.

items.producto: Shovels and buckets for removing mud
items.descripcion: Remove mud and standing water after the water has passed.
Prevents mold and structural damp after flooding.

secciones.titulo: Communication and alerts: when the network goes down
secciones.intro: In a DANA, coverage is the first thing to fail: if your mobile loses signal and there is no power, this is what alerts you and keeps you connected. Everything works without mobile signal or installation.

items.producto: Battery or hand-crank FM/AM radio with built-in flashlight
items.descripcion: Mobile networks and power go out just when information is needed most. Buy a radio with a large dial, note the regional station and Radio Nacional on the cover, and test it once a month: official alerts are still broadcast on radio and over municipal loudspeakers. Keep spare batteries separately, outside the device.

With mobile networks down, two people 300-500 m apart in a flooded town can still talk: PMR446 radios are legal in Spain without a license, with common-use channels. They are useful so one person can queue at the distribution point while the other stays with someone who cannot move. How to use them, in the PMR446 guide on the blog.

items.producto: External battery (power bank) 10,000-20,000 mAh, two outputs
items.descripcion: Without power, your phone is your flashlight, your map and your contact with family: it runs out in hours. Charge it to 100% when the orange alert is issued and don't use it up on videos; with a small solar panel or the car charger you can top it up again. Keep the short cable in the same bag.

items.producto: FFP2 mask (pack) and protective goggles for cleaning
items.descripcion: Flood mud carries sewage and, when it dries, it gets inhaled: when removing mud and knocking down wet walls, wear a mask and cover your eyes. Use it on the first day, not when it already smells. If you have asthma or breathing problems, do it with another person present and take breaks.

kit-apagon.titulo: Blackout Kit: 15 items to get through a power cut (2026)
kit-apagon.resumen: Blackout Kit: 15 items to get through a power outage. Guide based on the EU Preparedness Strategy (2025).
kit-apagon.coste_total: 90-200 € for the essentials; 257-525 € with all the recommended items (SAI, solar panel, fire extinguisher...) — in addition to the basic kit
kit-apagon.paraQuien: For everyone. On 28 April 2025 the peninsula went 12 hours or more without power: traffic lights out, ATMs closed, lifts stopped, supermarkets without card payment terminals. A long blackout is not a minor anecdote: it is a day without being able to buy, without water on upper floors and without a lift.
kit-apagon.paraQuien_no: It won't help if what you expect is to keep working or studying as normal: that requires the ability to generate electricity (a large panel, a home battery), which is another level of investment. And if you live on a fifth floor without a lift, bear in mind that the water you go down to fetch has to be carried back up on foot.

antes: Charge phones and power banks daily if there is a warning of grid strain
Keep cash at home: card payment terminals don't work without power
A gas burner or camping stove to eat something hot
Put two frozen bottles of water or gel blocks inside the freezer: on the day of the outage they go into the fridge and give you hours of cold without opening the door.
Test your CO detector today with its test button and check that the fire extinguisher gauge is in the green. In a blackout there is no time to discover they don't work.
durante: Don't use candles as your main light source: always use a flashlight
Unplug sensitive appliances to avoid surges when the power comes back
Save phone battery: calls and SMS only (the data network may go down)

No combustion appliances in a closed room: no braziers, barbecues, generators or gas stoves inside the home or garage. If you light the stove, cross-ventilate (one window and another opening) and keep the CO detector in sight.
Sort the fridge by thawing order: milk, meat, fish and cold cuts first; frozen and canned goods last. Anything already thawed gets cooked or thrown out: don't refreeze.
With a UPS, turn off the computer and leave only the router: you keep wifi while the battery lasts and avoid the voltage spike when power comes back.
despues: Recharge everything again and restock what you used
Check food that has lost the cold chain
Before going to sleep, air out the room where you used a flame and check the CO detector and fire extinguisher again.
Restock what you used: batteries, candles, freezer gel and anything you opened from the pantry. The next outage won't warn you.

errores: Opening the fridge every so often to see what's inside. Kept closed, a fridge holds for about 4 hours and a full freezer for up to 24-48 hours.
Lighting candles and leaving them unattended: the classic cause of home fires during blackouts. With kids, a flashlight, period.
Not unplugging appliances: when power returns, the surge can fry the fridge, the boiler or the router.
Relying on your phone having battery: during blackouts everyone calls at once and the antennas don't hold up long. Airplane mode and a full power bank.
Paying by card and discovering the card terminal doesn't work. Cash in small bills is the plan, not the detail.

secciones.intro: One light per person, and not candles. Magnetic lamps hang inside the fridge or cupboard and change everything.

items.producto: Rechargeable LED lights with magnet (for fridge/pantry)
items.descripcion: Sticks to the fridge, pantry or car hood. Hands-free.
Lights without tying up your hands: essential for working at night.

items.producto: Emergency candles (backup only, with a safe candle holder)
items.descripcion: Light backup, never the main source. With metal candle holder.

secciones.intro: Keep your phone and radio alive for 3-4 days. Large power bank, small panel to recharge it and a dynamo charger as a last resort.

items.producto: Power bank ≥ 20,000 mAh with AC output or USB-C PD
items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh external battery: 4-5 full phone charges.
Recharges the power bank with sunlight. 20-40 W charges a phone in 3-4 hours.
Hand crank: infinite power without sun or grid.

secciones.intro: Being able to make a coffee or heat water makes all the difference to morale during a blackout. And it means doing it in a ventilated area: butane in an enclosed space kills.

items.descripcion: Hot food without electricity. Always use in a ventilated area.
Protein and calories without refrigeration. Prioritize legumes and fish.

items.producto: Ice packs (freezable gel blocks) for fridge and freezer
items.descripcion: Keep them frozen in advance: on the day of the outage they go into the fridge, next to the most perishable items (meat, fish, dairy, cold cuts), and extend the cold hours without you having to open the door to check anything. Equivalent free trick: two frozen water bottles. And anything that has already thawed is not refrozen: cook it or throw it away.

secciones.intro: A blackout changes how you cook and how you light your home, and that brings two invisible risks: carbon monoxide and fire. They are two small purchases that are almost never used and that, on the day they are needed, are the only ones that matter.

items.producto: Battery-powered carbon monoxide (CO) detector with alarm
items.descripcion: CO has no smell, is invisible and does not irritate: it causes drowsiness and headaches and, if you stay in the room, it kills you in your sleep. During a blackout people light candles, burners and braziers, and that is where it appears. Put it at head height, outside the bathroom and near the cooking area, and press the test button every time the clocks change. Non-negotiable rule: braziers, barbecues, generators and burners never in a closed room or in the garage.

secciones.intro: Cash, a paper contact list and a radio. When everything is digital, analogue decides.

items.descripcion: Store cash and critical documents at home.
The only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. Better with a hand crank.

items.producto: Small UPS (600-900 VA) for router and ONT
items.descripcion: A 600-900 VA SAI keeps the router and ONT running for as long as its battery lasts (usually minutes, not hours) and, as a bonus, protects the equipment from power surges when the power comes back. Connect only the router: if you also plug in the computer or TV, the battery runs out quickly. It is not a generator: it does not power a fridge, heating or washing machine.

kit-coche.titulo: Car Kit 2026: DGT mandatory and optional items
kit-coche.resumen: DGT mandatory car kit 2026: V-16 beacon, vest and all the essentials. Verified list and Amazon cart in 1 click.
kit-coche.coste_total: 60-120 € (not counting the V-16 beacon, which is mandatory)
kit-coche.paraQuien: For drivers, which is almost all of us. Beyond what is legally required, it is what you need if you break down on a mountain pass in January, in a 6-hour traffic jam in August, or waiting for a tow truck at 3 in the morning.
kit-coche.paraQuien_no: It is not a workshop kit: if you expect to change a wheel yourself or recharge a battery, you also need a jack, lug wrench and jumper cables, and to know how to use them. And it does not replace the backpack you carry inside: the car may end up where you do not want to be.

antes: Check tires, battery and fluid levels before long trips
Check the condition of the kit at every change of season
durante: If you break down, signal from inside the car with the approved connected V-16 beacon: it is the only legal means from 1/1/2026 (RD 159/2021; DGT, note of 25/11/2025). Triangles are no longer valid
Do not get out of the car in snow if there is traffic: inside is safer and warmer

From 1/10/2026, when passing a vehicle stopped due to a breakdown or accident, reduce the road speed limit by at least 20 km/h and leave 1.5 m of lateral separation; in traffic jams, open a central emergency lane for ambulances and tow trucks (RD 518/2026, of 24 June, BOE-A-2026-13889, published 26/06/2026)

From 1/10/2026, wearing a seat belt is always mandatory: the reform of the General Traffic Regulations removes the exemptions for taxi drivers, delivery drivers and driving school instructors; only patients in an ambulance on emergency service are exempt (RD 518/2026, art. 119.2, BOE-A-2026-13889)

From 1/10/2026, on motorways and dual carriageways where the road is made difficult by snow, overtaking is prohibited and you must drive in the right-hand lane (the adjacent one if there are three or more), leaving the left-hand lanes free for snowploughs and emergency services (RD 518/2026, art. 32 of the General Traffic Regulations, BOE-A-2026-13889)
despues: Restock what you have used (batteries, water, fuel) when you get home

errores: Not checking the V-16 beacon: the connection expires (it usually lasts about 12 years from manufacture) and some models are not DGT-approved. Triangles are no longer valid from 1/1/2026.
Having the kit in the boot and the boot full of stuff from the last move. A covered-up first-aid kit doesn't exist.
Not checking the spare wheel or the water level: a puncture 30 km from the nearest petrol station is a problem that lasts hours.
Relying on your phone with 8% battery and no power bank in the car.
In snow, setting off without chains or not knowing how to fit them. Textile snow socks are a legal stopgap in some places and a danger in others: find out beforehand what your area allows.

secciones.intro: What they can require of you in an inspection or in an accident. Since 1/1/2026 the connected V-16 beacon is the only legal signalling device.

items.descripcion: From 1 January 2026 they are no longer valid for signalling in Spain (they are replaced by the connected V-16 beacon); still useful for trips to countries outside the Vienna Convention.

items.producto: Approved connected V-16 beacon (the only legal means from 1/1/2026)
items.descripcion: Mandatory since 1 January 2026: it replaces triangles. Only approved models connected to the DGT are valid (official list at dgt.es). Check the IDIADA/LCOE certificate engraved on the lens.

items.producto: High-visibility reflective vest (mandatory equipment on motorcycles)
items.descripcion: From 1/10/2026, motorcycles must carry a high-visibility reflective vest among their mandatory equipment in accordance with PPE regulations (RD 518/2026, Annex XII of the General Vehicle Regulations; BOE-A-2026-13889). For the car, it is still what keeps you legal if you walk along the hard shoulder at night.

secciones.intro: What you need if you have to spend the night inside the car or walk to an exit.

items.descripcion: Compact version of the basic first-aid kit, adapted for road traffic accidents.
Retains 90% of body heat. Takes up the space of a pack of cigarettes.
Attaches to the hood or bodywork. Hands-free for nighttime breakdowns.
For being towed or towing with emergency loops.

items.producto: Snow chains or textile snow socks
items.descripcion: Textile or metal. Mandatory on signposted snowy stretches.

secciones.intro: Water, some warmth and battery. In a snowy mountain pass or a summer traffic jam, it's what keeps your spirits up.

items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh external battery: 4-5 full phone charges.
Replace every 6 months: plastic degrades with the heat in the car.
Fast energy in a compact format. 400-500 kcal per bar.

kit-hogar.resumen: Home kit: 22 items for confinement and household emergencies. Guide based on official sources (EU + Civil Protection).
kit-hogar.coste_total: 210-420 € (2 people, 7-10 days, with stove, light, radio, power bank and CO detector)
kit-hogar.paraQuien: For anyone who wants to be covered without having to leave home: water outages, lockdowns, storms that isolate a neighborhood, or simply a week when you don't feel like or can't go out to buy supplies. It's the pantry stock, not the backpack.
kit-hogar.paraQuien_no: It's not for evacuation: if you have to leave in 15 minutes, this stays where it is. In that case, prepare the evacuation backpack with the essentials. And if you have a pet or baby, the reserve must include their supplies from day one, not when they run out.

antes: Calculate water and food for everyone in the household × 3 days
If there are children, babies or pets: tailor the kit to them
Keep games or books on hand to keep morale up
Keep a manual can opener and a tested butane stove: without them, your canned food is useless
Fill at least one bathtub with water for non-drinking use (toilet cisterns, cleaning) if the outage is imminent
Test the radio, flashlight and stove once a quarter and keep spare batteries of the same size: a kit with dead batteries is not a kit
Charge the power bank and check expiry dates every six months, on the same day you change the clocks: that way you'll never forget
durante: Ration water if the supply is cut off
Ventilate daily if possible
Keep the official radio on at least twice a day
Open windows for 5 minutes every few hours to refresh the air: accumulated CO2 makes you sad and slow
If you light a butane stove, candle or brazier, do it with ventilation and with the CO detector on: indoors, combustion consumes oxygen and carbon monoxide gives no warning
Phone in power-saving mode and with data off; call when you have coverage and save the powerbank for the radio and flashlight
despues: Inventory of what has been used and immediate replacement
Replace batteries, water and food consumed the same day, not the following week: the next emergency gives no warning
Write down what you missed during those days: that list, and no other, is your shopping list for the kit

errores: Buying things nobody eats at home. An emergency pantry is rotated by eating it, and if you don't like it, it doesn't get rotated.
Not having a can opener: if you have 30 cans and can't open them, you don't have food, you have a gym weight.
Not having a way to cook without electricity: twenty cans and an unlit stove.
Forgetting water for use: without a tap you can't flush the toilet. Filling the bathtub in time is free.
Storing everything together in a single cupboard: if one room floods or gets damaged, you lose the entire reserve.
Not adding the household's chronic medication to the plan: two weeks' reserve of treatment is the difference between sheltering in place and having to go out.
Using the phone as a flashlight: the most expensive light is the one that leaves you without battery to call
Storing batteries inside the radio or flashlight: they corrode and ruin the device just when you need it. Keep them separate, in their packaging

secciones.intro: The foundation of the pantry. A realistic quantity for the days you want to cover, and rotation so it doesn't expire.

items.descripcion: Food-grade container for storing drinking water. Allow 3 litres per person per day.
Protein and calories without refrigeration. Prioritize legumes and fish.

items.producto: Pasta, rice and legumes in packets
items.descripcion: Long shelf-life calorie base (2-3 years).
Don't forget them: extra ration for at least 3 days.

secciones.intro: When water is scarce, hygiene is the first thing to break down and the second thing to make you ill.

items.descripcion: Basic hygiene without guaranteed running water.
DANA floodwater leaves mud mixed with sewage: disinfect everything.
If water fails, the toilet won't flush: manage waste with bags.
Without running water, you can't flush the toilet or wash. Sealable bags to manage waste hygienically until the tap comes back on.

secciones.intro: If the power goes out and you can't cook, the 20 cans in the cupboard are useless without a can opener. Always have a way to prepare hot food.

items.producto: Portable butane stove with gas canisters
items.descripcion: Heat water and cook canned food and soups without electricity. Always use it in a ventilated area.
Without electricity, an electric can opener won't work. A manual one for 5 € is the most underrated tool in the kit.

items.producto: Cooking pot or sturdy saucepan (to heat canned food)
items.descripcion: You can heat empty cans with water and put the canned food inside (a homemade bain-marie) or use a saucepan to heat water if the power is out.

This kit recommends a butane stove indoors: CO has no smell, is invisible and can kill while you sleep. Place it at breathing height, in the kitchen or wherever you cook, and never turn it off to save batteries.

secciones.intro: Thermometer, antiseptic, general painkillers and whatever your doctor prescribes. With no pharmacy open, the first-aid kit is the pharmacy.

items.descripcion: To detect fever when you can't get to a doctor immediately.
Basic painkillers and fever reducers. Check the expiry date annually.
Protection against dust, smoke or a respiratory outbreak.

secciones.intro: Three days without power with a child at home and nothing to do can feel long. The psychological side also needs preparing.

items.descripcion: Morale matters: 72 hours confined can feel endless with nothing to do.
Entertainment without batteries or a network.

secciones.intro: Without forced ventilation during confinement, the air gets polluted quickly. Two simple measures prevent headaches and fatigue.

items.descripcion: Moves air if heat builds up. Runs off the kit's power bank for hours.

items.producto: Portable CO2 or air quality monitor
items.descripcion: CO2 that builds up in a closed home causes drowsiness, headaches and reduces your ability to think. A cheap sensor alerts you.

secciones.intro: A lockdown kit with no light and no radio depends on a phone that dies within hours. These three devices are what keep the household informed and visible when the power goes out.

items.descripcion: Without light you can't find anything and you end up using your phone as a flashlight — the very thing you need to make calls. Keep spare batteries of the same size, stored outside the devices.

When the mobile network goes down, the radio still broadcasts official alerts with no internet and no phone battery. Tune in the local stations before you put it away and test reception where you plan to use it.
With your phone at 20% you have two calls left. A charged power bank gives you several full charges and powers the radio or fan over USB. Recharge it every six months even if you don't use it.

kit-montana.titulo: Mountain kit: 15 essentials for outdoor survival (2026)
kit-montana.resumen: Mountain kit: 15 essentials for outdoor survival. Navigation, shelter, water and communication with no network. Practical guide 2026.
kit-montana.coste_total: 105-205 € (you probably already own much of it if you run or cycle)
kit-montana.paraQuien: For anyone who goes hiking, canyoning or mountain skiing. 90% of mountain rescues in Spain involve people who lost their way, got injured or were caught out by nightfall. You don't need to be an expert: going a little further than planned is enough.
kit-montana.paraQuien_no: This is not high-mountain gear: for glaciers, via ferratas or overnight stays at altitude you need technical equipment and training. And if you head somewhere with no coverage, this kit won't keep you in contact: phones don't always work, and the real solution is to tell someone your route and your expected return time.

antes: Always share your route and return time with someone
Check the weather warning (AEMET) before setting out
Download the 112 app for your region
Never wear new shoes or socks on a long hike: 74% of pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago get blisters in the first few days (Colexio de Podólogos de Galicia)
durante: If you get lost, stay put and make yourself visible
Ration your water and don't stray from the known route
Use trekking poles if you can: they cut impact on knees and ankles by up to 30%
If you feel rubbing: stop and apply the hydrocolloid dressing before a blister forms (Compeed, Scholl or similar)
despues: Replenish and check the kit after every outing
Note down what you were missing for next time
Dry and store the raincoat: moisture builds mold and it loses its waterproofing

errores: Going out in city clothes and trusting the weather app. In the mountains the temperature drops by 10 degrees as soon as you climb above a ravine, and fog can arrive in 20 minutes.
A single flashlight for the group, with no spare batteries, at the bottom of the backpack.
Not carrying an extra layer 'because I'm doing the route in two hours': half an hour waiting for rescue in a gully happens at zero degrees.
Drinking little and arriving at the end dehydrated and with heatstroke, especially in spring with sun and a backpack.
Relying on your phone for navigation. It runs out, gets dropped, gets wet. Map and compass, and know how to use them before you need them.

items.descripcion: 3 litres in 92 g. It fits into any gap in your pack and takes up nothing when empty. Takes 42 mm threaded filters (Katadyn BeFree) and handles hot water up to 60 °C.
They turn stream or spring water into drinking water in 30 minutes, with no filter or battery.

secciones.intro: Knowing where you are and being able to call for help. A whistle can be heard much farther than your voice and doesn't tire you out. Add paracord for lashings and improvisation.

items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh external battery: 4-5 full phone charges.
It can be heard from 1 km away; your voice, from 100 meters. No batteries needed.

items.producto: Physical map and compass of the area
items.descripcion: Classic navigation never fails. Learn to use it before you set off.
4 mm rope, 250 kg strength. Useful for lashing your backpack, improvising shelter, immobilizing or helping another walker. Not for climbing.

secciones.intro: What prevents hypothermia if you have to stop and wait for hours.

items.descripcion: Double-sided: orange to be seen, silver to retain heat.
Hypothermia kills in the mountains even in summer.
30% of body heat is lost through the head.

secciones.intro: Wound closure strips, cuts, blisters and broken gear: the small surgery of the route.

items.descripcion: Bandages, medical tape, blister care, basic immobilization material.

items.producto: Sunscreen and lip balm with protection
items.descripcion: SPF 50: radiation in the mountains is much higher than at the beach.
64% of medical consultations among walkers are for blisters. Apply them at the first sign of rubbing, before the blister appears. Compeed or similar.
Cuts, saws, opens cans and repairs gear. The hiker's Swiss Army knife.
Needles, thread and mini scissors in a compact case. For repairing a backpack, clothing or a rain jacket torn mid-hike.
Hands-free for walking at night or repairing gear.

kit-calor.resumen: Heat kit: 7 life-saving items in a heatwave — hydration, cooling and sun protection. From 30 €, and you already have most of them.
kit-calor.coste_total: 30-70 € (you already have most of the items)
kit-calor.paraQuien: For households without air conditioning or with power cuts during a heatwave, and for anyone who has older people, babies or people with chronic illnesses at home. Spain has weeks above 40 degrees, and heatwaves are the natural hazard that causes the most deaths, almost all preventable.
kit-calor.paraQuien_no: It is not a beach or hiking kit: in those settings, what matters is shade, a hat and water. And it does not replace real prevention: if your home reaches 35 degrees at night, the kit helps, but the plan is to go somewhere cool.

antes: Close blinds and sun-facing windows during the day
Drink water even if you are not thirsty; avoid alcohol and caffeine
Check on older neighbours and vulnerable people

Follow AEMET warnings and ES-Alert alerts on your mobile phone: the Basic Directive on adverse weather phenomena (BOE, 27/04/2026) establishes them as the main warning channel. The National Action Plan for Excess Temperatures is active from 1 June to 15 September
durante: Stay in the coolest room in the house
Lukewarm showers, not cold ones
If you feel dizzy, have a headache or have dry, hot skin: it could be heatstroke, call 112
despues: Check whether anyone's medication needs refrigeration and have a plan B

errores: Drinking a lot of water on its own on days with heavy sweating, without salts. Hyponatremia (low salt) causes dizziness and confusion and is mistaken for heatstroke itself.
Pulling down the blinds late. When the house is already at 33 degrees, opening south- and west-facing windows lets the heat in.
Leaving anyone in a parked car: in 15 minutes the interior rises by more than 20 degrees. Pets too.
Relying on a fan when it's over 35 degrees: it moves hot air and dehydrates you. From that point on you need to cool the body, not the air.
Ignoring the older person who lives alone and says they're fine. Heatstroke in older people causes confusion, not thirst: they don't ask for help.

secciones.intro: Cooling the body without electricity: towels, battery-powered fans and a spray bottle are worth more than they seem.

items.descripcion: Moves the air when the heat is stifling. Runs on a power bank.
Wet it and it lowers body temperature through evaporation. Reusable.
Spray cold water on the skin: immediate relief for mild heatstroke.

secciones.intro: Water plus salts, and knowing how much. An insulated bottle with ice in the morning gives you cold water at night.

items.producto: Steel insulated bottle (keeps cold for 12-24 h)
items.descripcion: Keeps water cold for 12-24 h even at 40 degrees.
They replenish mineral salts lost through sweat. What drinking water alone doesn't fix.

secciones.intro: Sunglasses, hat and sunscreen. The day-2 burns during a heatwave are from going out for 20 minutes 'to run an errand'.

items.descripcion: Serious burns dehydrate you even more. Reapply every 2 hours.
Real UV protection, not cosmetic. Your eyes burn too.

kit-evacuacion.titulo: Evacuation Kit: 14 items to escape alive (2026)
kit-evacuacion.resumen: Evacuation kit: 14 items to escape alive. Lightweight backpack with the essentials in 30 seconds. Quick preparation 2026.
kit-evacuacion.paraQuien: For when they tell you 'get out of your house now' —a fire, a chemical explosion, a flash flood— and you come back in 3 days, or in a month. It's the only thing you take in your hands, so decide now what goes inside, not when the alarm sounds.
kit-evacuacion.paraQuien_no: It's not the holiday suitcase or the long-stay kit: it's designed to survive 72 hours away from home, not to live for a week in a sports centre. And if you have reduced mobility, a large pet or a baby, this backpack has to be shared out and tested beforehand.

antes: Backpack in the hallway, always in the same place
Copy of documents in a waterproof bag
Evacuation route agreed with the family
Spare house keys in the backpack: in a panic it's the first thing people forget
Test the backpack by walking 5 km with everything inside: that's the only way to know whether it carries well and what you're missing
durante: Don't go back home for things you forgot
Follow only the instructions of the emergency services
If you have to move on foot, wear closed, comfortable shoes: the ground may be covered in glass and debris

If you evacuate at night or with poor visibility along an interurban road, wear the reflective item: from 1/10/2026 it is mandatory for pedestrians on the carriageway or hard shoulder (RD 518/2026, art. 123, BOE-A-2026-13889)
despues: Do not enter your home until you are officially authorised
Always wear protective footwear and gloves when handling debris: mud and debris after a flood or fire can be contaminated
Check the backpack every 6 months: update expired medication, food and documents

errores: Leaving it in the storage room or in the car: if you are evacuating at night from your bed, the backpack has to be in the hallway, hanging up, with everything inside.
Packing clothes for a month. It weighs 12 kilos, your shoulders hurt at 4 km and you end up leaving things behind along the way. 30-40 L and under 8 kg.
Not testing it: walk 5 kilometres with it one Sunday. It's the only way to know what you're missing and what you don't need.
Not including spare keys, documents and a rechargeable phone card that doesn't depend on your own line.
Forgetting small cash and a charger: in the first days, the queue to recharge your phone is the most repeated scene in any disaster.

secciones.intro: What can't be replaced for months: ID, deeds, policies, medical cards, on paper and on USB.

items.producto: Waterproof folder or pouch for documents (ID, deeds, policies, prescriptions)
items.descripcion: ID, deeds, policies, health card and prescriptions in one place.

items.producto: Digital copy on an encrypted USB
items.descripcion: Backup of scanned documents. Encrypt it with a password.
A spare set kept in the waterproof folder. In the panic of an evacuation it's the first thing people forget: you go back home and can't open the door.

secciones.intro: Water, food, warm clothing and somewhere to shelter while you are relocated.

items.descripcion: Water-resistant, with padded belt. It will carry you through 3 days.
They purify questionable water in 30 minutes. Vital if bottled water runs out.
At least 2 rations per person in the backpack.
A warmth and rain-protection duo in a minimal format.

secciones.intro: Radio to find out what's happening, a light to move around, a knife for repairs and a whistle to call for help, a first-aid kit for treating wounds, and cash to buy things when cash is all there is.

items.descripcion: Minimal power kit: to see and communicate.
Mini but complete version: gauze, antiseptic, painkillers.
During an evacuation, ATMs don't work. 10-20 € notes.
The only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. With a dynamo so it never goes silent.
Three blasts are the international emergency signal. It can be heard farther than your voice and never runs out. Essential if you get trapped.
23 tools in a compact body: knife, saw, screwdrivers, bottle opener. Just enough for emergency repairs.

items.producto: Luminous or reflective element for walking at night (mandatory for pedestrians)
items.descripcion: From 1/10/2026, anyone walking on the roadway or shoulder of an interurban road between sunset and sunrise, or in reduced visibility, must wear at least one luminous or reflective element in accordance with PPE regulations, visible at 150 m (RD 518/2026, art. 123 of the General Traffic Regulations, BOE-A-2026-13889). In a night evacuation after a DANA or fire, it is the difference between being seen and not.

huerto-autosuficiencia.resumen: Self-sufficient garden: 13 tools to grow your own food: seeds, compost, autonomous irrigation and protection. From 50 € to get started; 300 € already set up.
huerto-autosuficiencia.coste_total: 50-200 € to start well (seeds, substrate, trays, tools) — up to 300 € with compost bin, mesh and irrigation.
huerto-autosuficiencia.paraQuien: For those who want the next step: stop depending on the shopping cart and understand where their food comes from. Starting with a balcony and sprouts is realistic, cheap and addictive. It is also your food insurance: a few kilos of well-stored seeds provide food for a year.
huerto-autosuficiencia.paraQuien_no: It's not a real self-sufficiency plan for a family on its own: living off a garden requires land, water, time and two or three years of learning. And if you don't even have somewhere to put a plant pot, put together the basic kit first: it's more urgent and cheaper.

antes: Look at your space: how many hours of direct sun it gets per day (at least 4 h for tomatoes; 2-3 h is enough for lettuce and herbs)
Start with what is easy and productive: lettuce, arugula, chard, herbs, radishes
Prepare the calendar: in Spain, spring sowing runs from February to April; autumn for spinach, garlic and onions
Set up a home composter: kitchen scraps feed the garden. A 20 L bucket with a tap costs 25-35 € and prevents smells
Cover windows with aphid-proof mesh (2x8 m, 10-20 €): without protection, whitefly and thrips can destroy a balcony garden in two weeks

Check your residents' association rules or housing portal: in some buildings (especially rentals), pots are banned on balconies or shared terraces. If they are allowed, ask about maximum weight and watering.
Buy pots with saucers: the saucer catches irrigation water and prevents stains on the floor of the entrance or communal terrace. Without a saucer, no one will let you keep the garden.
durante: Water first thing in the morning or at dusk, never in direct sun
Loose, well-draining potting mix: a pot without holes is certain death for any plant
Add fertilizer every 2-3 weeks with compost or liquid fertilizer
If you use drip irrigation, check the drippers every week: they clog easily, and a dry plant is not noticeable until it is too late
Check the aphid mesh after storms: if it is torn, replace it. A 2 cm hole is enough for whitefly to get in
If you grow in pots, renew the potting mix each season: after one season it has lost nutrients and become compacted. About 5-8 € per pot and two new harvests.
despues: Harvest from the outside (outer leaves) so the plant keeps producing
Save seeds from your best plants for the next cycle
Note down what worked and what did not: your garden notebook is your best tool

errores: Starting with 20 varieties and a large garden. It gets abandoned in six weeks. Start with three things you eat: tomatoes, lettuce, herbs.
Sowing by the calendar instead of by your climate: sow when your valley's temperature allows it, not when the table says.
Using cheap discount-store potting mix or garden soil in pots: it compacts, doesn't drain and you kill the roots.
Not having a guaranteed water supply: in a balcony vegetable garden, a weekend away without watering is a dead garden.
Storing seeds without drying them and without a date: after two years nothing will germinate. Airtight jar, label, cool dark place.

Throwing kitchen scraps in the bin: a 20 L compost bin costs less than 35 € and turns that waste into free fertilizer. The right ratio is two parts browns (dry leaves, cardboard) to one part greens (food scraps).
Relying on insecticides without netting: whitefly reproduces in two weeks and insecticides kill bees. Cover first, treat afterwards.

secciones.intro: Seeds, trays, potting mix and a meter. For less than 60 € you get half a year of salads, sprouts and well-watered cherry tomatoes.

items.descripcion: Tomato, pepper, eggplant, zucchini and more, with certified organic seeds. The best starting point.
Seed tray to get strong plants started before moving them to pots. Reusable, recyclable material.
Soil with built-in fertilizer, suitable for practically any container vegetable.

secciones.intro: Three quality pieces are worth more than a fifteen-piece kit that breaks.

items.descripcion: Rake, transplanting trowel and hoe from a long-established Spanish brand. Just the essentials.

items.producto: 6 L watering can with detachable rose
items.descripcion: Soft rose for seedlings and a direct stream for mature plants.

secciones.intro: Mini greenhouse and reading when you've already killed your first tomato and want to understand why. With compost and watering, the garden goes from hobby to real production.

items.descripcion: Extends the season and protects from the cold on a balcony or terrace. Fits in any corner.

items.producto: Urban and organic gardening manual for beginners
items.descripcion: From zero to a full garden: how to turn a terrace or garden into food, step by step.
The benchmark illustrated guide: sowing calendar, companion planting, pests.

kit-30-dias.titulo: 30-Day Kit: 16 items for a month without supplies (2026)
kit-30-dias.resumen: 30-day kit: 16 items for a month without supplies — 180 L of water for 2, pantry, cooking and personal care without power. 300-500 € that you recoup by eating it.
kit-30-dias.coste_total: 300-500 € (2 people, and much of it is recouped by eating it)
kit-30-dias.paraQuien: For those who have covered the 72 hours and want to take the next step: a week without being able to buy anything, a region cut off by a DANA, a long blackout or a lockdown-type event. At this stage it is no longer a backpack; it is a pantry and a plan.
kit-30-dias.paraQuien_no: This isn't anyone's first kit: if you don't have the 72-hour kit put together, start there — it covers 95% of real scenarios and costs a fraction. And with 30 days, you don't get 30 days of medical self-sufficiency or endless water: work out how to get water and how to reach a doctor before stockpiling food.

antes: Calculate actual consumption: 2 people, 30 days = 60 L of drinking water + 40–60 L for basic hygiene
Prioritize food you already eat: an emergency pantry you don't rotate is money thrown away
Store everything in a cool, dark, dry place; write purchase dates on each pack
Add your household-specific items to your kit: regular medication, diapers, pet food
durante: Start consuming by expiry date: fridge first, then freezer (if kept closed, it holds for 24–48h), then pantry
Ration water per person, not per day: 3 L/day per adult for drinking is the minimum
Cook with the stove in a ventilated area, never inside a closed room
despues: Restock what you consume the following week, marking the dates again
Check that cans aren't bulging or rusty and replace them
Note what was left over and what was missing: adjust quantities for the next review

errores: Buying 30 days of food and not being able to cook it: without gas or electricity, raw rice is decoration. Secure a cooking method and fuel first.
Not calculating water: 3 L per person per day is 180 L for two people for a month. It's what runs out first and takes up the most space.
Not rotating. A pantry you don't touch is garbage in three years; one you eat from day to day never expires.
Not accounting for the bathroom: without water, 96 rolls are not enough and hygiene becomes the household's sanitation problem.
Doing it all at once and at the worst price. Build it over 4–6 months by adding two packs per shopping trip, and it costs half as much.

secciones.intro: The real bottleneck of the month. Large containers with a tap, rotation and a plan for making water safe to drink.

items.producto: 8 L jugs with a dispensing tap (x8 = 64 L)
items.descripcion: Bezoya 8 L with tap: convenient for dispensing. Calculate 3 L/day per person for drinking and cooking.
The jug from your local supermarket works just as well. Also store bathwater if there is advance warning.

secciones.intro: What keeps you going: canned goods and ready meals that are eaten cold and need no cooking.

items.producto: Light tuna in water (pack of 6 cans)
items.descripcion: Cheap, long-lasting protein. Multiply packs according to the days covered.

items.producto: Lentejas a la riojana Litoral (pack of 6)
items.descripcion: A complete ready-to-eat meal; can be eaten cold if there is no way to heat it.
Calories and protein in a single jar. A very good energy-to-price ratio.
Mussels, sardines, cockles… varying the flavours keeps morale up in a long crisis.
Easy to eat without cooking, on toast or on its own. Long shelf life.

secciones.intro: Rice, pasta, pulses and powdered milk. Cheap, calorie-dense and with a shelf life of years.

items.descripcion: The quintessential long-life food. Buy 6-8 kg for the month.
Makes ~7 litres of milk per bag. Vitamin D and calcium without a fridge.

secciones.intro: A cooking method is what turns a pantry into hot meals. Always in a ventilated space.

items.descripcion: Takes a standard butane cylinder or a small cartridge. Use only in a ventilated area.
For the cold during a winter blackout. Triple safety system. Always ventilate.
If the home becomes uninhabitable, or to isolate a room and retain body heat.

secciones.intro: Paper, soap, a complete first-aid kit and vitamins. What keeps health and morale going for weeks.

items.descripcion: Dressings, bandages, antiseptics, gloves, medical tape. The health basics for 30 days.
It is one of the first things to disappear from supermarkets at any warning.
Covers gaps if your emergency diet is monotonous (no fresh fruit or vegetables).
Nutrient-dense superfood, high in protein and micronutrients, with a very long shelf life.

kit-bebe.titulo: Baby Kit: 32 essentials to protect your child (2026)
kit-bebe.resumen: Baby kit: 32 emergency items — feeding without power, hygiene, warmth and documents. From 90 €; you already have most of it: rotate, don't duplicate.
kit-bebe.coste_total: 90-170 € (much of it is what you already use daily: rotate it, don't duplicate it)
kit-bebe.paraQuien: Households with babies aged 0-18 months, and also anyone expecting one: it takes two afternoons to put together and pays off just as much in everyday use. If you breastfeed, much of this kit is extra peace of mind; if not, it's essential.
kit-bebe.paraQuien_no: If your child already eats everything on their own, the basic kit plus two or three things from here (snacks, entertainment, warmth) is enough. This kit is designed for infants, not older children.

antes: Write down on paper the baby's medication/feeding schedule and your paediatrician's phone number: in an emergency, not knowing what they take is a mess
Keep a bottle and a training cup that you never use: they're spares, so they're not in the dishwasher on the day you need them
Keep photocopies of the baby's ID/health record and vaccination card in the waterproof pouch
Talk to your family: who takes the baby if you have to evacuate quickly? Decide roles now

Write the opening date on the lid of the formula tin and set a reminder for 25 days: once opened, it should be used within about 4 weeks (as stated by the manufacturer); it won't last until the printed expiry date. Rotating it is what makes the kit work.
durante: With a baby in your arms, the evacuation backpack is split: someone carries the child, you carry the baby's 24-hour bag
If you're not sure you'll be able to breastfeed calmly, express milk with a manual pump in the first few days so you don't lose your supply
Watch the baby's temperature: without power there's no room thermometer, feeling the back of the neck and chest is misleading, use the thermometer from the first-aid kit
Doubtful water for the bottle: boiling isn't always possible — purify and cool, or use low-mineral bottled water kept in reserve for infant feeding

Powdered formula: prepare it just before feeding (AESAN recommends using it within 2 hours) and throw away any leftover from a bottle the baby has already fed from. With ready-to-use liquid formula, you don't have that clock.

If you can't boil: sterilize with cold-water sterilizing tablets and rinse with drinking water. And if the baby is under 28 days old, was born premature or with low birth weight, AESAN says to use boiled water and add the powder to water above 70 °C (check the label and with your pediatrician).
despues: Check for bumps and knocks: babies can't tell you, so any unusual change in behavior or sleep means see the pediatrician
Restock what was used the same day: a diaper and milk reserve that isn't replenished is a half-finished kit
If the crisis was long, ask your health center to check your vaccination card and bring it up to date if needed

Restock with the current size and dose, not those in the kit: the baby changes every month. And if during those days there was fever, vomiting or fewer wet diapers than normal, tell your pediatrician before considering the episode over.

errores: Not having RESERVE FORMULA: milk supply drops with stress and without 2-3 days' formula, that causes double the anxiety. Even if you breastfeed, put 400-800 g of formula on the list.
Relying on always being able to boil water: without gas or electricity you can't sterilize bottles — you need a dedicated drinking-water bag and a cup, not just a bottle.
Not counting diapers: a baby uses 6-8 diapers a day. 72 hours is ~20 diapers: a small bag that almost nobody includes.
Keeping a new puree the baby has never tried: in an emergency, give food you already know they tolerate.
Forgetting the 'next size up' coat: the baby grows and the coat outfit in the kit becomes too small at 3 months without anyone noticing.

Keeping the bottle the baby hasn't finished for the next feed. With powdered formula you throw away what's left: it's the most common mistake in an emergency and the one that causes the most gastroenteritis in a baby.
Leaving liquid formula in the trunk or storage room: heat degrades it before the expiry date. Powder, however, does not go in the fridge (moisture makes it clump): cool and dry, not cold.

secciones.intro: Bottles and baby food require safe water and temperature. Without electricity or gas, you get this with your own reserve and a small butane heater.

items.descripcion: For preparing baby bottles without purifying the water: look for low mineral content (sodium <20 mg/L), the type recommended for infants.

items.producto: Water purification tablets suitable for infants
items.descripcion: Plan B for tap or rain water when bottled water runs out. Only use them with clear water and leave the full resting time.

items.producto: Baby bottle warmer without gas or electricity (chemical/self-heating)
items.descripcion: Bags that warm a bottle in minutes without fire. For lukewarm porridge and water at the right temperature in a car or a sports centre.
Keeps water hot for mixing porridge or warming the bottle for hours. Wide mouth: easy to clean and easy to fill with a spoon.
Safe cold water for the baby during a heatwave, and to keep expressed milk for a few hours if there is no fridge.

secciones.intro: Even if you breastfeed: stress and exhaustion can reduce supply just when there is nowhere to buy. The reserve is insurance, not a doubt about your breastfeeding.

items.descripcion: A 2-3 day reserve even if you breastfeed. Check the expiry date every 6 months and rotate it by using it in porridge or cooking.
They are made with lukewarm or cold water, go a long way and need no cooking. The one your baby already has: don't try a new brand during the emergency.
Real food without cooking, with a long date. If they already eat purées, they are your kit and their dinner in a blackout.
No batteries or electricity, it keeps supply going and prevents painful engorgement if the baby cannot feed well (floor, car, field hospital).
For expressing and storing with the date. Without a freezer they last a few hours in a cool bag with ice packs.

secciones.intro: When running water is unavailable, baby hygiene is the first thing to become difficult. Everything in this section fits in a 5-liter waterproof bag.

items.descripcion: 6-8 a day: 20 diapers are 3 days. Write the size and date on the bag; a baby will outgrow the size before you move house.
Duo packs: diaper and face without water. In an emergency you use more than you think: seal the pack well or they dry out in a week.

items.producto: Waterproof bags for dirty clothes and diapers (pack)
items.descripcion: One for dirty items, one for clean clothes. Without a washing machine and with a child, keeping clean and dirty separate is worth its weight in gold.
A thin foam mat: it wipes clean, dries, and on the floor of a sports hall or car it saves you half a dozen arguments.
With a diaper on all day and limited water, diaper rash appears within 48 h and nobody sleeps well.
It goes further than liquid soap when water is scarce and also works for washing bottles and little hands.

secciones.intro: A baby loses heat five times faster than an adult. Without light or heating, this section is the one that prevents an emergency.

items.producto: Warm one-piece sleep sack/pajamas (current size + one spare)
items.descripcion: Better than loose blankets: it doesn't come off while they sleep and leaves your hands free for babywearing.

items.producto: Child emergency thermal blanket (or small fleece blanket)
items.descripcion: Don't leave the silver thermal blanket loose near the face: use it under the normal blanket or as a wind barrier in the carrycot.
They lose heat through their head that they cannot compensate for. At home with no heating at 16 °C, the baby sleeps with a hat.

items.producto: Ergonomic baby carrier (sling or Mei Tai)
items.descripcion: Hands free for the flashlight, backpack and door. In an evacuation, a baby carrier is worth more than a stroller: there are no elevators or sidewalks.

secciones.intro: The baby's first-aid kit plus whatever keeps a small child's spirits up for 48 hours shut in or in a strange place.

items.descripcion: Yours will do, but keep it dedicated: with no light and a scare, being able to take a temperature in 10 seconds saves a night of doubt.

items.producto: Oral rehydration solution and dosing syringe
items.descripcion: With vomiting or diarrhea from bad water, a baby dehydrates fast: early hydration and see the pediatrician. Follow your pediatrician's or nurse's guidance, not the internet.
Babies can't blow their noses themselves: with mucus they won't eat or sleep. And saline works for eyes, wounds and general cleaning.

items.producto: Favorite small toys (2-3, in a waterproof bag)
items.descripcion: The usual ones, not new: in a strange place with strange lights, what's familiar is what calms the baby.
That little blanket that smells of home. If it gets lost in an evacuation it's a three-hour drama: keep an identical one in the kit.

secciones.intro: A baby doesn't carry an ID, can't say their name and has no visible health card of their own. Their whole identity fits in a waterproof pouch.

items.producto: Waterproof pouch with the health record book, vaccination card and the baby's ID/passport
items.descripcion: Photocopies + originals if you have them. With a small child and no safety net, a piece of paper with their date of birth and allergies solves a lot.

items.producto: Child ID card (name, date of birth, blood type, allergies, contacts)
items.descripcion: A laminated card in the backpack and a recent printed photo of the child. If they get separated from you during an evacuation, this is what identifies them.

items.producto: Recent printed photos of the baby and the family
items.descripcion: It sounds old-fashioned and it works: in a shelter, a photo in your wallet is worth more than a phone with no battery.

kit-mayores.titulo: Senior Kit: 27 items to protect people who depend on others (2026)
kit-mayores.resumen: Senior kit: 27 items for people who depend on others — chronic medication, assistive devices, fall prevention and adapted food. From 60 €, not counting prescription.
kit-mayores.coste_total: 60-120 € (not including the medication itself, which is prescription-only)
kit-mayores.paraQuien: Households with people aged 70 or over, especially if they live alone, take chronic medication or rely on hearing aids, glasses or assisted mobility. A family member puts it together in an afternoon and it is checked against the prescription folder.
kit-mayores.paraQuien_no: It does not replace telecare or the carers' plan: it is equipment, not a service. And if the person needs daily health care (oxygen, dialysis), the plan is discussed with their health centre, not with this list.

antes: Make the medical ID card with the person: illnesses, medication with doses, allergies, doctor, contacts. It is updated every 6 months at the review.
Ask the doctor or nurse for a 2-week plan of chronic medication: in Spain, the electronic prescription allows most treatments to be collected in advance; your doctor will tell you how.
Practise using the card and the telecare phone number with the person, not just in front of them: in an emergency, 'they already know' is not enough.
Agree with neighbours and family who calls whom and what warning signal you use (call, message, knocking on the wall: during power cuts some people use a whistle).

Count how many times they get up at night to go to the toilet: if it is more than once, the urinal with a handle, a night light in the hallway and a non-slip mat come before any other product on the list.
Keep the medication in a bag with a handle that the person can hang over their shoulder, not in stacked boxes: when leaving quickly, people only grab what they can pick up with one hand.
durante: Medication first: if you have to decide, chronic treatment is not skipped; the kit's reserve is for that.
With hearing aids without batteries or broken glasses, the person becomes isolated and disoriented: check that they can hear and see before anything else.
Heat or cold: older people regulate temperature worse and don't notice thirst. In a heatwave with no power, keep water in sight and set a drinking schedule, even if they don't ask.
Don't let them make decisions alone if they are confused: heatstroke and dehydration cause confusion before weakness sets in.

Without a washing machine or hot water, incontinence is the day-2 problem: use incontinence pads and a separate bag for dirty clothes. Don't hand-wash with your reserve water: that water is for drinking.

If the phone fails and she lives alone, a whistle and rhythmic knocks on the wall are how a neighbor can locate her. Agree this beforehand with the neighbor and with her, using a specific signal (three knocks, pause, three knocks).
despues: Check used-up medication and restock the kit the same day with the prescription.
Check hearing aid batteries, pacemaker if applicable, and flashlights: after a scare, many things get used without being replaced.
Talk to the health center if treatment was interrupted: sometimes it has to be prescribed again.
Encourage them to talk about what they went through: after a long emergency, an older person's emotional crash is as real as a burst pipe.

Check the skin in folds and pressure areas if they have been unable to wash for more than 24 hours: any irritation or red area that doesn't recover should be discussed with their nurse or doctor, not treated at home.
Write down which product was actually missing and restock it that same day: the kit is corrected by what was used, not by what you thought you would use.

errores: Not having 2 weeks of reserve chronic medication. That is THE mistake: after a disaster, the pharmacy opens late or doesn't open, and stopping anticoagulants, antihypertensives or insulin is an emergency.
Forgetting hearing aid batteries: without hearing, the person doesn't hear the radio, doesn't understand the warning and doesn't ask for help. A blister pack of spare batteries in every kit.
Trusting the mobile phone: small screens, small print and no one to help them dial. A landline without electricity still works (analog ones do), and paper contacts don't run out.
Not preparing for a fall: without power, a carpeted hallway with no night light is a broken hip. LED night lights cost 10 € and prevent 50% of the scenario.
Store everything in the high kitchen cupboard. If you evacuate, the oldest person's 24-hour bag must be within easy reach, with their name and contact details.

Do not overlook incontinence. Without a washing machine or hot water, a single day without enough spare supplies forces a choice between hygiene and drinking water. It can be sorted with 15-30 € in the cupboard long before it is needed.

secciones.intro: The heart of this kit. Three things: a 2-4 week supply, a copy of the medication schedule and a way to keep anything that needs cold at the right temperature.

items.producto: Weekly pill organizer (pillbox) with a copy of the medication schedule
items.descripcion: Filled from the kit's reserve. If another person has to administer the medication, the pillbox + the record card prevent mistakes.
Medical conditions, treatment with doses, allergies, blood type, doctor, contacts. One copy in your wallet, another in your backpack, another on the fridge.

items.producto: Small cooler with reusable ice packs
items.descripcion: For insulin and medication that needs to be kept cold: with spare frozen packs it lasts 24-36 h. Check with your pharmacist which medications need it.
2-4 °C or throw it away. A 4 € thermometer tells you whether the insulin is still valid after the power outage.

items.producto: Water purification tablet and measuring cup for medication
items.descripcion: For taking tablets with safe, measured water. A small detail you'll appreciate on day 2.

items.producto: Battery-powered upper-arm blood pressure monitor with memory
items.descripcion: If someone in the household has diagnosed high blood pressure, the plug-in one is useless in a power outage. This one runs on batteries and stores the latest readings, so you can write them on the record card. Your doctor or nurse decides what values are normal and when to measure: this section only covers the device.

secciones.intro: Hearing aids, glasses, pacemakers, prostheses: if these fail, everything else in the kit becomes useless, because the person cannot hear the alert or see the door.

items.producto: Spare hearing aid batteries (blister × 3, with date)
items.descripcion: Hearing aid batteries run down and expire. Sealed blister with the date written on it: no batteries, no hearing, no communication.

An old pair of glasses in good condition or your prescription written down so you can order another pair. They fall and break right then; with the prescription in the drawer, half an hour at an online optician.

items.producto: Denture box + adhesive and a cup with a lid
items.descripcion: If they wear dentures: without spare adhesive and without a cup to keep them in overnight, they don't eat. A detail nobody considers.

items.producto: Folding cane / spare walker with light
items.descripcion: The cane stays in the other room when you need it. A light one in the hallway with built-in night light.

items.producto: Magnet or safety pouch for pacemaker (device information and card)
items.descripcion: The pacemaker card with model, center and phone number goes in the document sheet. In MRIs, CT scans and rescues, they ask for it and can't find it.

items.producto: Engraved medical ID bracelet or necklace (name, phone, allergies)
items.descripcion: With cognitive impairment or disorientation, in an evacuation the first thing lost is the wallet with the papers. An engraved bracelet or necklace with name, a relative's phone number and allergies can be read without unlocking anything or opening any pocket, and it doesn't expire or run out of battery.

secciones.titulo: Falls, night-time and safety at home
secciones.intro: A blackout doesn't kill an older person: the rug in the dark and the bathroom at night do. 20 € on a night light and a non-slip mat change the prognosis.

items.descripcion: They plug into the hallway and bathroom sockets and run on an internal battery: with no power, they light up without pressing anything. The night-time fall is THE avoidable accident.
The big, easy ones, not the small one in the drawer: with clumsy hands or in the dark, it should be findable and turn on by itself.

items.producto: Non-slip bath mat and support grab rail
items.descripcion: Without hot water and with buckets around, the bathroom becomes an ice rink. 20 € and an afternoon of DIY.
If they can't shout or the mobile phone doesn't work, a whistle is heard through walls much more than a voice. Teach them to use it beforehand.

secciones.intro: That they can call for help and that someone knows they are alone. Half the danger for an older person in an emergency is that nobody misses them for hours.
