items.producto: Battery-powered FM radio with high volume and large dial
items.descripcion: Official information without relying on your phone. Practise using it once a month so it doesn't become an unfamiliar object.

items.producto: Contact sheet on paper in large print (112, family, doctor, neighbor, pharmacy)
items.descripcion: Taped to the fridge and the bedside table. A phone with the numbers saved is useless if they don't know how to unlock it or can't find it.

items.producto: Neighbor agreement with a warning call/knock
items.descripcion: A designated neighbor calls or stops by every morning during a crisis. It's not an object; it's the most effective measure on the whole list: write it down on the record sheet.

items.producto: Playing cards, a large-print book or a radio with a speaker
items.descripcion: Three days shut in without company are easier with something to do. And morale is health too: it shows in who eats and who doesn't.

secciones.intro: Without a washing machine and without hot water, what at home would be solved with one wash becomes the problem of day 2. Here are the three things that preserve the most dignity and protect the skin best in an older person when services are out.

items.producto: Incontinence underpads and diapers (pack for 3-5 days)
items.descripcion: If there is incontinence, it's the first thing to run out and the last thing you can improvise: without a washing machine, without hot water and with the bathroom dark, there's no homemade replacement. Size and absorbency should be adjusted with their nurse or at the pharmacy, not by guesswork.

items.producto: Bedpan or urinal with a handle
items.descripcion: With reduced mobility or no light, the nighttime trip to the bathroom is the expected fall. A bedpan with a handle and a night light are enough so they don't have to get up in the dark. Empty and clean it with cleaning water, never with the reserved drinking water.

Older people lose heat faster and notice it less. The gold blanket doesn't give off heat by itself: it reflects the body's heat. It works much better inside a normal blanket, not on its own on top. It costs less than a coffee and fits in any drawer.

secciones.intro: Without a kitchen, without knives and sometimes without dentures: the kit food must be something that person can eat given the state of their mouth and their strength.

items.producto: Ready-to-eat soft food (purees, adult pureed food pots, creamed foods in tubs)
items.descripcion: If they have chewing problems, a can of preserved food is no good: purees and adult pureed pots can be eaten straight from the pot.
Calories and protein without cooking or chewing. In a 3-day crisis this is what keeps an older adult's weight stable.

items.producto: Thickeners for liquids (if dysphagia has been diagnosed)
items.descripcion: Someone with dysphagia, in an emergency, swallows air along with the drink and chokes. Follow their speech therapist/doctor's guidance: only your professional can prescribe this.

items.producto: Bottle with handle and easy-drink spout + cup with lid
items.descripcion: Drinking unaided, without spilling, using one hand. Dehydration in older adults appears without thirst: keep water within reach and easy to use.

kit-mascotas.titulo: Pet Kit: 23 items to protect your animal (2026)
kit-mascotas.resumen: Pet kit: 23 items to protect your animal in emergencies. Food, identification and first aid.
kit-mascotas.coste_total: €40-90 (€20-40 if you already have a carrier and bowl)
kit-mascotas.paraQuien: For any home with a dog or cat. In an evacuation due to fire, flood or smoke, the animal cannot stay behind and there isn't always room for it: the difference between taking it with you and losing it is having the carrier and leash findable within 30 seconds.
kit-mascotas.paraQuien_no: This is not a kit for leaving the animal alone at home for three days: an animal cannot manage itself like a pantry. If your emergency plan involves leaving and abandoning it, that plan doesn't work.

antes: Keep the carrier and leash in the same place as your emergency backpack, not in the storage room
Work out the water: about 50-60 ml per kilo per day (a 15 kg dog drinks almost 1 litre a day; a cat, 200-300 ml)
Keep a paper copy of the vaccination record and the microchip number: they ask for it at a shelter or refuge
Take a recent photo of the animal with you and keep it on your phone and on paper: it's what proves the animal is yours
If your dog needs a muzzle because of a potentially dangerous breed, keep it next to the leash: without it they won't let it on certain types of transport
durante: Animals sense fear: speak normally, don't pick it up if it's large, put it in the carrier without fuss
Offer water every 2-3 hours; stress dehydrates more than heat
Don't improvise with human food: sudden diet changes cause diarrhoea right when there's no vet
If there's smoke or gas, wet a towel and cover its snout without fully covering the nose
despues: Refill the animal's water the same day: it's the first thing drunk and the most often forgotten
Check legs and pads (glass, staples, burns) when you get home
Wait a few days before bathing it: its own scent gives it a sense of security in a new place
Note what it lacked (food it didn't like, uncomfortable bowl) and fix it before next time

errores: Thinking the animal will eat when it's hungry. A scared dog or cat leaves the kibble. Offer it wet food and sit with it; don't leave it alone with a bowl.
Taking it without a carrier 'because it's very good.' A scared cat and dog bite and run off; in an evacuation, a loose animal is a lost animal.
Forgetting the animal's water in the count. The family calculates 3 liters per person and forgets that the dog is another consumer.
Not carrying the vaccination record: without vaccines they won't accept it in shelters or boarding facilities, and it may not be able to pass certain checks.
Leaving it at home with water and food for 'two days.' With no ventilation, no shops and a damaged building, two days can be the last days before it falls off the list of things that are fine.

secciones.intro: What your animal drinks and eats for three days. With no shops open and no fridge.

items.producto: Water for the animal (reserved 8 L container)
items.descripcion: A medium dog drinks about 1 liter a day and a cat about 250 ml. The container is separate from yours: don't compete for water.

items.producto: Extra pet food (kibble or cans for 72 h)
items.descripcion: A closed reserve in plain sight, not half an open sack. Kibble or cans, whatever it already eats: an emergency is not the time to change diet.

items.producto: Collapsible travel food and water bowls
items.descripcion: They take up no space and stop it drinking from a dirty makeshift bowl. With them you can give it water at a stop in the car.

items.producto: Wet canned food (adds water and it will eat it when stressed)
items.descripcion: A scared animal rejects dry kibble but usually accepts canned food. The moisture helps it hydrate without drinking.

secciones.intro: If you have to leave in a hurry, this is what decides whether it comes with you.

items.descripcion: With a door that closes securely. A loose cat in an evacuation won't be recovered: it hides under the first car.
With the leash on and a second one as backup. In panic a dog breaks its usual leash and runs toward the road.

items.producto: Muzzle (if required or if he's nervous around strangers)
items.descripcion: Required for PPP breeds and necessary if he's going to be surrounded by frightened people. A muzzled dog can get on any transport.

items.producto: Blanket or towel with his home scent
items.descripcion: A new place is a threat to an animal; his blanket is the only sign that he's safe. It also works as a coat.
A lightweight alternative to a rigid carrier for rabbits, guinea pigs or small puppies.

secciones.intro: What lets you get through a checkpoint, a shelter or a border with him.

items.producto: Vaccination card and a copy of the microchip in a waterproof folder
items.descripcion: Up-to-date vaccinations and microchip number: it's the document that proves the animal is yours. On paper, because your phone can run out of battery.
Insulin, heart medication, anti-epileptics, antiparasitic. If the animal takes something daily, the backpack holds a month, not a week.

items.producto: Basic veterinary first-aid kit (gauze, saline, povidone-iodine, bandages)
items.descripcion: Cuts on paws, burns or irritation of eyes and ears. Saline solution cleans wounds and eyes without causing damage.

items.producto: Digital thermometer (shared with the general first-aid kit)
items.descripcion: It works for the animal and for people. Fever or hypothermia are measured the same way.

secciones.intro: Living with him for three days in an enclosed space without it being too noticeable.

items.descripcion: The same ones you use at home, but with a reserve: you won't be able to go down to the street for bags.

items.producto: Litter tray and cat litter (or pee pads)
items.descripcion: A stressed cat without a tray holds its urine and ends up at the vet. The disposable tray lasts two days.
For transport or the shelter: they protect the boot and surfaces if he can't hold it.
Paws, stuck-on litter and dirty fur without needing water. They work for him and for you.

secciones.intro: If he gets loose or if you have to go to different places, this is what lets him come back.

items.producto: ID tag with your phone number engraved
items.descripcion: A microchip has to be read with a scanner; anyone can read a tag. In an emergency with overwhelmed staff, the tag is faster.

items.producto: Recent photo of the animal with you (paper and phone)
items.descripcion: It is the most effective proof of ownership when there are no documents and whoever picks it up doesn't know you.
An animal that doesn't sleep and won't stay still is a problem in a shelter. Its toy calms it more than any command.

secciones.titulo: Plan B: who looks after it if you can't
secciones.intro: The part almost nobody writes about and the one that actually gets used the most.

items.producto: Agreement with a trusted person (with keys and the animal's record card)
items.descripcion: I'm in hospital, away or can't get there: someone with keys who knows where the food and carrier are and who knows the plan.

items.producto: List of boarding kennels and hotels that accept animals
items.descripcion: In an evacuation, not all shelters accept pets. Write down three places that do, with phone numbers, in your municipality and in the neighbouring province.

items.producto: Animal data protection (digital copy of vaccinations with the microchip visible)
items.descripcion: Phone photos of the vaccination card, saved on an encrypted USB stick and in the cloud: if someone asks for it remotely, you have it.

kit-frio.titulo: Cold/Winter Kit: 27 items to survive the cold (2026)
kit-frio.resumen: Cold kit: 27 items to survive extreme winter. Alternative heating, warm clothing and cold management 2026.
kit-frio.coste_total: €80-180 (half that if you use the winter clothing you already have)
kit-frio.paraQuien: For homes with gas or electric heating (both fail in a blackout), for anyone living in a snow or frost area, and for older people and babies, who lose body temperature before anyone else. Filomena left half of Spain without heating and unable to leave the house.
kit-frio.paraQuien_no: It is not a mountaineering or extreme mountain snow kit: that requires technical gear and training. Nor does it replace the basic rule: if you can't keep the house above 15 degrees, the plan is to go somewhere warm.

antes: Check you have a carbon monoxide detector before using any combustion appliance indoors (heaters, burners, generators): CO has no smell and no colour and kills in closed rooms
Prepare a «refuge» room: the smallest one with the fewest windows, to heat it and have everyone live there instead of trying to heat the whole house
Store the draught excluders/window sealing film before it freezes: sticking them on at -4 degrees won't hold
Put the winter kit in the car before the snowfall, not during it (check that the chains are your size and the tyres aren't low)
Check on older neighbours: cold indoors isn't noticed, it builds up
durante: Never use a combustion heater or stove in a room without ventilation: leave a gap open and turn the appliance off before sleeping
Dress in layers (thermal, liner, windproof) and cover your head, hands and feet: that's where more than half the heat is lost
Drink water even if you're not thirsty: in the cold you drink less and dehydration makes hypothermia worse
Don't go out to clear snow on an empty stomach or in wet shoes; and don't take the car without a scraper and full visibility
If you have to sleep at low temperature, do it in pairs and fully dressed: share the sleeping bag or blanket
despues: Check and clean the CO detector and restock batteries and fuel the same day: the second wave usually arrives within a week
Suspect frozen pipes: open the taps slowly before turning on the boiler; a pressure surge will burst the system
Restock salt, fuel and spent batteries: in snow, whatever runs out runs out across the whole region at once
Check the state of the car (battery, antifreeze, tyres) as soon as you can get out

errores: Using the stove or heater in a closed room. It is the leading cause of CO poisoning in blackouts and snowstorms: the appliance consumes oxygen and gives off carbon monoxide.
Trying to heat the whole house. Without heating you don't heat a house, you heat one room: choosing a small one and closing off the rest is the difference between 12 and 18 degrees.

Dressing the baby or the older person "with one more layer" of cotton. Over cotton you need a layer that cuts the wind and stays dry; and older people must be moved out of the house when their hands turn cold and pale.
Storing the power bank and the phone in the car. Cold kills their battery: at 0 degrees they lose up to half their charge and don't recover well.
Going out into the snow without a reflective item or a scraper. Most deaths in snowstorms aren't from cold, they're from traffic accidents and pedestrians being hit.

secciones.titulo: Body heat: the layer that saves lives
secciones.intro: Without heating, your clothes are your home. And not just any clothes: wet cotton makes you cold.

items.producto: Thermal base layer (top and leggings, 2 sets)
items.descripcion: The layer closest to your skin matters most: thermal fabric breathes and dries, cotton stays wet and steals heat.
Second layer: traps the body's warm air. Wool keeps you warm even when slightly damp.
Cold feet are the first warning sign of hypothermia. Wool handles sweat much better than cotton.
A huge amount of heat is lost through your head. Day and night, indoors too.

items.producto: Warm gloves (and thin ones for tasks)
items.descripcion: Without hands you can't do anything: not cook, not open a frozen tap, not use your phone. Two pairs, one thin pair underneath.

items.producto: Warm one-piece sleeping bag or pyjamas (current size + one spare)
items.descripcion: You won't sleep at 10 degrees in light pyjamas. A one-piece garment stops air getting in when you move.
Reflects body heat. It doesn't provide warmth on its own: you have to wrap yourself in it, not lay it on top like a sheet.

secciones.titulo: Safety: the silent enemy is CO
secciones.intro: When the heating fails, people improvise with combustion indoors. That's where disasters happen.

items.producto: Battery-powered carbon monoxide (CO) detector with alarm
items.descripcion: Effectively mandatory if you're going to use any combustion appliance. CO has no smell, can't be seen, and won't wake you: it kills in your sleep.

items.producto: 1–2 kg ABC dry powder fire extinguisher with bracket
items.descripcion: Heaters and cables overloaded by demand are typical fire sources in a winter blackout.
If you run a generator or an extension lead to an electric heater, this device is the difference between a blown fuse and a fire.

secciones.intro: Heat one room, not the whole house. And always with ventilation and a detector.

items.producto: Butane gas heater with oxygen depletion cut-off
items.descripcion: The most effective option for a small room. It requires a gas cylinder, ventilation and a CO detector. Never for sleeping.

items.producto: Camping gas stove with canisters (for hot water and food)
items.descripcion: Hot water and hot food raise your body temperature faster than any heater. Use outdoors or with a window open.
A hot drink every two hours is the cheapest way to keep the body warm. The thermos keeps it hot for 6 hours.
Lighting the stove or burner with cold hands and gloves on is difficult. Long matches prevent burns.

secciones.titulo: Keep the cold out: the home
secciones.intro: Seal the house tightly so you can heat just one room.

items.producto: Tape and plastic to seal windows and gaps
items.descripcion: A poorly sealed old window lets as much heat escape as a small stove can produce. Ten euros of plastic is worth more than turning the stove up.

items.producto: Thermal curtains or a wool blanket to cover the window
items.descripcion: At night, covering the glass is the cheapest improvement: glass is the coldest surface in the home.
A cold, damp home feels 3-4 degrees colder and ruins clothes. Humidity is half the problem of a winter without heating.

secciones.titulo: Outside and in the car: snow
secciones.intro: Filomena did not leave people without heating: it left them unable to leave home and unable to use the car.

items.producto: Ice scraper and snow brush for the car
items.descripcion: Driving with just a clean rectangle on the windshield causes thousands of accidents with every snowfall. And you have to clear the roof: the slab slides off when you brake.

items.producto: Snow chains or textile snow socks
items.descripcion: On a motorway in snow, you must drive in the right-hand lane, and the left lanes are kept clear for snowplows (art. 32 RGC). Without chains you cannot get up a mountain pass.

items.producto: Snow shovel and de-icing salt (or sand)
items.descripcion: For getting out of the parking space and for the sidewalk. Salt also prevents ice from forming at the front door.

items.producto: Jump leads and antifreeze with protection down to -25
items.descripcion: Cold kills the battery and freezes the coolant circuit. They are the two No. 1 failures during a cold snap.

items.producto: Approved connected V-16 beacon (replaces warning triangles)
items.descripcion: In fog or snow, getting out to place warning triangles is dangerous: the beacon is placed from inside the car and has been the only legal means since 1/1/2026.

items.producto: Light or reflective item for walking at night
items.descripcion: Mandatory for pedestrians on the shoulder of an interurban road at night or in poor visibility (art. 123 RGC). In snow, a reflective item visible at 150 m is the only thing between you and a car.

secciones.intro: In winter it gets dark at 18:00 and a power outage leaves the house dark and without heating.

items.descripcion: With gloves on and in the dark you need both hands. A headlamp is the only useful light for moving around a cold house.
Snow warnings and closed roads come over the radio when the mobile network is overloaded or the antennas have no power.
Note: cold reduces capacity by up to half if you store it in the car. It goes inside the house, in an inner pocket if you go out.
Radio, flashlight and CO detector run on batteries. A CO detector with no batteries is just an ornament.

kit-terremoto.titulo: Earthquake Kit: 26 items for seismic protection (2026)
kit-terremoto.resumen: Earthquake kit: 26 items to protect you from falling objects and glass, shut off gas and water and call for help. Light, first-aid kit and cash: from 90 €.
kit-terremoto.coste_total: 90-170 € (much of it overlaps with the basic 72-hour kit)
kit-terremoto.paraQuien: For people living in a seismic zone (mainland southeast: Murcia, Almería, Granada, Málaga, Alicante) and, in fact, for any home: most damage in an earthquake is not from the quake itself, it is from falling objects and gas and power cuts. The kit is the same one that serves you for a power outage.
kit-terremoto.paraQuien_no: It is not a rescue or rubble kit: it doesn't turn you into a firefighter. Nor does it replace structural reinforcement or knowing whether your building is one that holds up: that can't be solved with a backpack.

antes: Anchor shelves, the TV and tall wardrobes to the wall: the No. 1 cause of minor injuries in an earthquake is things falling from walls
Locate the gas and water shut-off valve and check that it turns: after the earthquake you'll have 30 seconds and shaking hands
Leave closed-toe shoes and a flashlight next to the bed (under the bed, tied together): at night, broken glass on the floor is the biggest cause of cuts
Agree on a meeting point outside the building and a contact outside the province: local lines get overloaded, outside ones don't
Keep the backpack near the exit door, not in the basement storage room
durante: Drop, cover under a sturdy table and hold on to the furniture: the furniture moves with you and protects you from falling objects
Don't run out to the stairs or use the elevator: most injuries happen while fleeing and in stairwells
Move away from windows, mirrors, shelves and façades. If you are outside, go to an open space away from cornices and cables
If you are in a car, stop in an open area, not under a bridge, streetlights or power lines
If you smell gas, do not turn anything on: no lights, no matches, and no mobile phone near a leak
despues: Put on closed-toe shoes before walking around the house: broken glass is the leading cause of injuries and you cannot see it in the dark
Shut off the gas and water if there is a smell or damage, and do not turn on switches if you suspect a leak
Wait and listen to the radio: aftershocks are the norm in the following hours, and instructions come via radio stations and ES-Alert
Do not enter damaged buildings or use the elevator; check the structure before staying (new cracks, doors that will not close)
Record damage with photos and report it to your insurer and the local council: aid is assigned by declared areas, and that requires documentation

errores: Running to the stairs as soon as the shaking starts. Most injuries occur while fleeing: in a stairwell, with people and with falling objects. The right place is under a sturdy table.
Sleeping without shoes nearby and without a flashlight at hand. A nighttime earthquake + glass-covered floor = cut feet and darkness, just when you need to get out and help.
Lighting a match, turning on the light or using your mobile phone when you smell gas. It is the spark that causes the explosion. Shut off the gas first, then everything else.
Not knowing where the gas shut-off valve is or not having a tool to close it. It is the first thing to do and almost no one has ever touched it.

Confusing “the house is still standing” with “the house is safe”. You need to check for new cracks, doors that will not close and damp before sleeping inside: aftershocks bring down what the first tremor left weakened.

secciones.titulo: Head and feet: what breaks first
secciones.intro: In an earthquake, what hurts you is not the ground, it is what falls. And that day you discover you are barefoot.

items.descripcion: Cornices, lamps, shelves and brick partitions can fall. A construction or bike helmet works and fits in the backpack.
For clearing rubble, glass and overturned furniture. Without gloves you cannot help anyone or clear your own exit.

items.producto: Sturdy closed-toe shoes next to the bed
items.descripcion: A pair of boots or hard-soled shoes tied under the bed. Walking barefoot on broken glass is the most avoidable injury in a night-time earthquake.

items.producto: Protective goggles (or sunglasses if you have nothing else)
items.descripcion: Dust, plaster and splinters get into your eyes. Sunglasses cover them and work as basic protection.

secciones.titulo: Water and food that needs no cooking
secciones.intro: The gas may be cut off, there may be no power and the water may come through cloudy. The rule is: don't cook anything that needs more than opening a container.

items.producto: Bottled water (3 L per person per day)
items.descripcion: Six 1.5 L bottles per person for 72 hours. The water network is one of the first things to break and one of the last to be repaired.
If the mains water runs cloudy or you have to use water from a tank, wait 30 minutes and it's drinkable. It weighs nothing and works for weeks.

items.producto: Ready-to-eat food that needs no cooking (tinned food, bars, nuts)
items.descripcion: Tinned food, nuts and bars: no need for gas or a camping stove. Cold, ready food is plan A after an earthquake.
Without power there's no electric can opener, and many tins don't have a ring pull. Five euros that can leave you with no dinner.

items.producto: Dehydrated or ration food (in case it drags on)
items.descripcion: Supplies that stretch beyond 72 hours: an earthquake with structural damage can mean weeks of disruption.

secciones.intro: If you're trapped or in the dark, this section is literally your voice.

items.descripcion: With rubble around and no light you need both hands. A head torch goes on your head and lets you dig, help and walk.
A whistle carries further than your voice and doesn't run out. Shouting for hours leaves you out of breath; a whistle doesn't. It's the cheapest rescue tool there is.
After an earthquake, radio broadcasts reach where the mobile network doesn't. It's your only source of instructions if the masts go down.
Your phone is your spare torch, your map and your way of calling for help. Without battery, none of that exists.
Radio, torch and gas detector run on batteries. Bring double the spares: in an emergency there's no shop.
If you end up waiting for rescue in the open or in a car, it's the only thing that prevents hypothermia. It takes up less space than a phone.

secciones.titulo: First aid kit, medication and wound care
secciones.intro: An earthquake causes cuts and bruises, not exotic accidents. And some people with chronic conditions can't skip a dose.

items.producto: Full first aid kit (gauze, bandages, antiseptic, scissors)
items.descripcion: Cuts and bruises. You need to be able to clean and bandage without going to the emergency department, which will be overwhelmed.

items.producto: Chronic medication (7-30 days) with a copy of the prescriptions
items.descripcion: People with diabetes, on anticoagulants, with hypertension, with asthma. If your medication is in a closed pharmacy, you have a serious problem within 24 hours.

items.producto: Pocket first aid kit to carry with you
items.descripcion: A small one with gauze and adhesive bandages for your pocket or bag: minor wounds can be treated on the spot.
With heat, dust, exertion and little water it's easy to get dehydrated. It also works for diarrhea.

secciones.titulo: Shut off gas, water and electricity
secciones.intro: The damage from an earthquake is multiplied by whatever is left open afterwards. This is the first thing to do and nobody has it to hand.

items.producto: Gas and water shut-off key (square or universal key)
items.descripcion: Without it you can't close the gas supply. After an earthquake, an open leak turns a scare into an explosion.
Pliers, screwdriver and blade in a pocket: cut through a jammed shutter or shut a valve when you have no tool.
To secure a door, lower something down, make an improvised stretcher or tie down a tarp. 30 meters of rope solves the unpredictable.

secciones.intro: What you need for the hours that follow: breathe without dust, prove who you are and be able to pay without a card terminal.

items.descripcion: Rubble and plaster dust irritates and damages the lungs. After an earthquake there is dust in the air for days.

items.producto: Waterproof folder or pouch with copies of documents
items.descripcion: ID, deeds, policies, prescriptions: if the house is sealed off or damaged, papers are the difference between claiming and being unable to prove anything.
With no power or network, the card terminal doesn't work and the ATMs are down. 100-150 € in 10 and 20 notes covers water, food and fuel.

items.producto: Digital copy on an encrypted USB
items.descripcion: Photos of the house and belongings before the earthquake: it's the evidence the insurer asks for to assess damage.

kit-incendio.resumen: Fire kit: 21 items for a wildfire — breathe without smoke, get out in 10 minutes, defend the house and evacuate those who can't run. From 60 €.
kit-incendio.coste_total: €60-140 (you already have most of it, or it works for other emergencies too)
kit-incendio.paraQuien: For anyone living in the wildland-urban interface (homes next to hillsides, housing estates, villages) or in areas of dry scrubland — an ever-growing share of Spain. And for anyone caught by surprise by smoke on the road.
kit-incendio.paraQuien_no: This is not a kit for staying behind to defend the house. If the authorities order an evacuation, a kit does not turn you into a firefighter or give you the right to stay: you evacuate.

antes: Clear 10 metres around the house: brush, firewood, dry grass and hedges against the façade are the fuel that carries the fire to your windows
Keep metal sheets or wooden shutters to cover the windows, and the backpack by the door, not at the back of the garage
Write down the municipal evacuation plan and the alternative route: in a fire, the road heading up into the hills is the first to be cut off
Walk the exit route in your head at night: if a warning wakes you at 3:00 with smoke, you won't be able to improvise
Work clothes and closed-toe shoes within reach: synthetic clothing melts onto your skin
durante: Evacuate as soon as there is an order or smoke in the air, carrying nothing beyond the essentials: a car is faster than a defended house
Close windows, doors and blinds to reduce draughts, and turn off ventilation and heating before you leave
If you are caught in the car: do not get out, wait with the windows closed, lights on and the air on recirculation; the car protects you better than running

If you are caught on foot: always move downhill and downwind (the fire climbs the slope faster than you can), head for an open area with no vegetation and, as a last resort, lie down on ground that has already burned
Cover your nose and mouth with a damp cloth and do not breathe through your mouth; smoke is more dangerous than the front line of flames
despues: Do not return until the authorities authorise it: burned ground still has hot spots and roots keep burning underground
When you get there, do not turn anything on until you have checked the installations: the service line and the meter are often damaged
Wet down the outside and check the perimeter for hours: embers flare up again with the wind
Report it if you suspect the origin, and keep photos of the damage for insurance and for the local council

errores: Staying to defend the house when the fire is already close. Houses are defended beforehand (by clearing brush and wetting them), not when the fire front is 200 metres away: from that point on, you only evacuate.
Taking the car towards the hills “because it's closer”. Fire climbs the slope and cuts off the road above first. The emergency exit is almost always downhill and downwind.
Wearing synthetic clothing and sandals. It's the combination that turns a brush with heat into a burn stuck to your skin and makes evacuating on foot impossible.
Shouting to warn someone far away. Smoke leaves you without air in minutes: use a whistle and a phone call, never run or shout.
Believing the danger ends when the fire front is out. Embers flare up again with the wind, and burnt trees and ground remain dangerous hours later.

secciones.titulo: Breathing: smoke kills before the flames do
secciones.intro: In a wildfire, almost all victims die from inhalation. This section matters most.

items.descripcion: They filter smoke particles: fine ash, soot and dense smoke. A few minutes of unprotected smoke and you become truly disoriented.
Smoke and sparks make your eyes water until you can't see the exit. Close-fitting goggles let you keep walking.

items.producto: Cotton cloths or towels (to wet and cover your mouth and nose)
items.descripcion: A damp cloth filters some of the smoke and cools the air. It's what people use when there is no mask, and it helps even if you have one.

items.producto: Water for drinking and wetting cloths (8–10 L bottle or container)
items.descripcion: Smoke dries your throat, and in heat and stress you drink less than you should. It also wets cloths instantly.

secciones.intro: An evacuation order doesn't give you an afternoon to get ready. Whatever isn't in this backpack stays behind.

items.descripcion: Already packed and by the door. If you have to fill it on the day, you're losing the minutes that count.

items.producto: Waterproof folder with documents and some cash
items.descripcion: ID card, deeds, policies, health card and cash in small denominations. Rebuilding everything without paperwork takes a year of paperwork.
Smoke cuts visibility to a few metres and night can fall. Keeps your hands free to carry, open and help.
Evacuation routes change with the wind. The radio gives you the current instruction when mobile coverage fails.

items.producto: Physical map of your area (roads, alternative exits)
items.descripcion: If the network is overloaded or there's no data, the paper map gets you out; GPS leaves you at the closed road like everyone else.
If you lose visibility in the smoke, a whistle is what lets them find you. It fits in your pocket.

secciones.titulo: Clothing that doesn't melt onto your skin
secciones.intro: What you're wearing decides whether the heat brushes past you or burns you.

items.producto: Long-sleeved cotton or wool clothing (not synthetic)
items.descripcion: Polyester and nylon melt and stick to the skin. Cotton and wool protect and can be wetted.

items.producto: Closed, sturdy footwear (boots or hard-wearing shoes)
items.descripcion: No sandals: burnt ground and embers go straight through a thin sole. And you can't run in flip-flops.
For opening a hot metal door, grabbing a hose or moving something that burns. Without gloves you can't touch anything.

items.producto: Cotton cap or scarf to cover your head and neck
items.descripcion: Radiant heat and embers come from above. Covering your head prevents burns to your hair and neck.

secciones.titulo: Defending the house if there's still time
secciones.intro: Only while there's no evacuation order. Ten minutes of preparation can save the house; one minute too many can cost you your life.

items.producto: Long reinforced hose (plus a sprinkler or spray nozzle)
items.descripcion: To soak the perimeter, the façade and nearby scrub. The most effective thing before the front arrives.

items.producto: 6 kg ABC powder extinguisher (or several 2 kg ones)
items.descripcion: For fires that reach the house: roof, stacked firewood or a vehicle. A car extinguisher isn't enough.

items.producto: Hoe, rake and manual brush cutter
items.descripcion: Clearing dry grass and leaf litter around the perimeter is what stops a ground fire reaching the façade.
Useful for putting out small flare-ups and soaking hot spots without a hose or power. Very handy when the electricity goes out and the pump stops working.

secciones.titulo: Animals and people who can't run on their own
secciones.intro: An evacuation is measured by the slowest, not the fastest.

items.producto: Pet carrier and leash to hand (pets)
items.descripcion: In a smoke evacuation, a loose animal hides or runs off into the hills. With a carrier, it leaves with you on the first trip.

items.producto: Chronic medication and a list of treatments (older people or dependants)
items.descripcion: Anticoagulants, insulin, inhalers, psychiatric treatments. They go in the backpack with a copy of the prescriptions, not in the bathroom cabinet.

items.producto: Spare cane, walker or folding chair
items.descripcion: Whoever walks slowly sets the pace; having a spare mobility aid stops the evacuation from getting stuck.

kit-comunicacion.titulo: Communication Kit: walkie-talkies, radio and satellite messenger (2026)
kit-comunicacion.resumen: Off-grid communication kit: licence-free PMR446 walkie-talkies, crank radio and satellite messenger. 6 items from 80 € so you never miss an alert.
kit-comunicacion.coste_total: 80-300 € (PMR446 walkie-talkies + battery radio and powerbank; more with satellite messenger)
kit-comunicacion.paraQuien: For any household that wants to be able to alert others and be alerted when every network goes down at once: a long blackout, a DANA storm, a fire or a lockdown.
kit-comunicacion.paraQuien_no: It doesn't replace your phone day to day, and it won't let you make long-distance calls without an amateur radio licence. And it's not a toy: if you don't test it beforehand, you won't know how to use it on the day of the emergency.

antes: Agree a fixed family channel and sub-tone (channel 7, sub-tone 7) and write it on each walkie-talkie
Test the real range: one at home and one out on the street; in the city it reaches far less than the box promises
Tune in and save the useful stations (regional and Radio Nacional) before putting the radio away
Keep spare batteries out of the devices and a short cable with the powerbank
If you have a satellite messenger, set up the emergency contacts and test sending a message
durante: Listen before transmitting: two stations at once block the channel with a screech
Short messages and speak slowly; repeat figures and addresses twice
Radio on at least twice a day to hear official warnings
Don't clog the mobile network with calls: texts get through when calls don't
Agree a fixed contact time so you don't drain the battery all day
despues: Recharge the walkie-talkies, powerbank and messenger, and replace used batteries
Note down what failed (range, channel with interference) and fix it
Check your satellite subscription if you have one: don't let it lapse

errores: Not testing the walkie-talkies beforehand: an unused device is an expensive brick.
Buying walkie-talkies that aren't PMR446: many cheap devices use bands that do require a license.
Relying entirely on the satellite messenger: if it runs out of battery, you're left unable to communicate.
Storing the batteries inside the radio: they corrode and ruin the device.
Calling instead of texting: in an emergency, voice calls fail before short messages.

secciones.intro: No license, no coverage and no internet. PMR446 radios have been legal in Spain since 1998 and let you talk radio to radio when there is no network.

items.descripcion: Pair of rechargeable PMR446 walkie-talkies. License-free 446 MHz band, common-use channels.
Better antenna and sensitivity: up to 5-10 km in open country.

secciones.titulo: Listen and alert the outside world
secciones.intro: When the mobile network goes down, the radio still broadcasts official alerts and satellite messages still get through.

items.producto: Battery-powered or hand-crank FM/AM radio (with flashlight)
items.descripcion: The only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. Hand-crank, no batteries.

items.producto: Power bank 10,000-20,000 mAh for your devices
items.descripcion: The rechargeable walkie-talkie and the phone die at the same time. Two ports keep them alive for several days.
Messages and SOS via satellite network where there is no mobile coverage. Requires a monthly subscription.
Stored inside the radio, they corrode. Keep them separate, in their packaging.

kit-starlink.titulo: Starlink kit: satellite internet for emergencies (2026)
kit-starlink.resumen: Starlink kit: satellite internet from anywhere (400-600 € + 50-60 €/month), backup 4G router and satellite messenger as a last resort.
kit-starlink.paraQuien: For those who live in areas without mobile coverage or fiber, for those who want real communications redundancy in an emergency, or for those who work in rural areas where the fixed network fails. Starlink works from any location with a clear view of the sky.
kit-starlink.paraQuien_no: Not for those who have mobile coverage and fiber that don't fail: there you can wait. It also requires ~100° of clear sky (trees and mountains cut the signal) and a monthly subscription: without it, the hardware is a brick.
kit-starlink.busc: Starlink portable terminal Gen 3 4G emergency router

antes: Check Starlink coverage in your area: the official app shows sky visibility and installation forecasts.
Check coverage from two different carriers at your location: redundancy only exists if both have signal.
Calculate the total budget: terminal (500-1.200 €) + subscription (45-60 €/month) + router (300-800 €) + inReach (~400 €).
Plan the location: a roof with 100° of visible sky or an outdoor mast of 2+ meters. Avoid balconies with obstructions.
durante: Activate Starlink and its subscription. Use the app to find the optimal installation point by scanning the sky.
Test the speed. Readjust if there is high latency (>100 ms) or packet loss.
Configure the 4G/5G router with dual SIM and automatic failover between the two carriers.
Activate the inReach and its plan; test sending a message and geolocation.
despues: Clean the Starlink panel every 2-3 months: dust, fallen leaves and droppings reduce the signal.
Renew subscriptions before they expire: when reactivating, the price sometimes changes.
Test the inReach every month: test message and geolocation. A drained battery doesn't save lives.
Check antennas and connections every 6 months: wind, rain and salt air corrode the contacts.

errores: Mounting Starlink with an obstructed view. It needs ~100° of clear sky; trees, roofs or mountains cut the signal. Use a roof or terrace with an open view, not the balcony.
Forgetting the monthly subscription. Without it, the terminal is a 500-1.200 € brick. Residential plan (50-60 €/month) or mobile plan (45 €/month).
Not having redundancy (Starlink + 4G/5G router). A single means of communication is a single point of failure: with extreme weather and no cellular coverage, you'd be cut off.

secciones.intro: Satellite internet when everything goes down: mobile phones, fiber, LTE. 50-200 Mbps real-world speeds without ground infrastructure. Gen 3: lower power consumption and better performance in adverse conditions.

items.descripcion: Satellite internet where there is no coverage or fiber. Real-world 50–200 Mbps. Gen 3: 75–150 W, built-in Wi-Fi. “Mobile in Transit” plan €45/month. The subscription is essential: without it, the hardware is useless.

items.producto: Mounting bracket for Starlink (roof / wall / mast)
items.descripcion: Robust bracket to secure the terminal to a roof, wall or mast while maintaining a clear view of the sky. Compatible with Gen 2 and Gen 3.

items.producto: Extension cable for Starlink (30 m / 60 m)
items.descripcion: Extends the cable to the ideal location. Shielded, resistant to UV, water and rodents. Compatible with Gen 2 and Gen 3.

secciones.intro: Cellular connectivity as Starlink backup: useful when satellite is not viable (dense forests, extreme weather) or as a secondary option.

items.descripcion: 12–16 dBi: amplifies the signal when coverage is weak. Roof installation with cable to the router.

secciones.intro: When there is no clear sky view or cellular coverage, a satellite messenger is the only way to call for help.

items.descripcion: SOS, geolocation and two-way messaging where there is no coverage. 90 h battery life in normal mode, 35 h active.
Keeps the inReach and phone charged when there is no power grid. USB-C charging.

kit-electricidad.titulo: Electricity Kit: 10 items to keep the lights on without the grid (2026)
kit-electricidad.resumen: Electricity kit: power for the essentials with a solar panel, SAI and cables — light, router and portable fridge with no mains. From 200 €.
kit-electricidad.coste_total: €100–250 (power bank + lights + batteries) up to €500–900 (with solar generator and LiFePO4 battery)
kit-electricidad.paraQuien: Any household that wants minimal lighting and communication when the power grid fails: apartments with a balcony (folding panel) or houses with a roof.
kit-electricidad.paraQuien_no: Does not replace a fuel generator for tools or air conditioning: that is a different level of budget and window requirements.

antes: Calculate your real wattage: add up the essentials (LED lights, router, phone, fridge if possible) and buy with some headroom.
Place the solar panel where it gets direct sun for most of the day; in winter it produces half as much
Charge EVERYTHING to 100% every Sunday: a battery at 60% on the day of the outage is a useless battery
Use LED lights with built-in batteries: they consume 10 times less than any alternative
Keep the cables together and labeled: in the dark there's no time to check which is which
durante: Power lights, phone and radio first; the fridge only if your generator can handle the start-up surge
The router uses very little: keeping the internet alive can be worth more than a fridge
Recharge during the day with the panel; draw from the battery at night: never both at once
Turn off and unplug what you don't use: devices on standby drain the battery and give you nothing in return
despues: Recharge everything to 100% again before storing the kit
Note down how many hours it lasted and what you used: next time you'll buy better

Using candles unattended: it's the leading cause of fires during power outages.

kit-kit-profesional.titulo: Professional Kit: total power and autonomy (2026)
kit-kit-profesional.resumen: Professional kit: 800 W of solar panels, 19.2 kWh LFP batteries, SAI and Starlink to get through a long blackout without interruptions. Cost and installation 2026.
kit-kit-profesional.paraQuien: For households that can't afford to be left without power, data or food: rural homes far from services, businesses that depend on servers, or anyone looking for real independence from blackouts and infrastructure crises.
kit-kit-profesional.paraQuien_no: It is not a kit for surviving months off-grid. High investment (2.000-5.000 €), it needs space (roof or land for panels, a ventilated area for batteries and generator) and professional installation, and it requires maintenance. It is not 'install and forget'.

antes: Calculate your daily consumption: kWh/month ÷ 30 = kWh/day. The kit should cover 70-80% of that consumption.
Identify where to install the panels: south-facing roof, flat roof or adjacent land. Minimum 4 m² for every 400 W.
Prepare the battery space: ventilated area, 10-25 °C, away from flammable materials.
Locate the generator spot: outdoors, ventilated, 3+ metres from windows, with access for refuelling.
If you don't know how to install it: budget for an electrician + certified solar installer. It's not witchcraft, but it has to be done right.
durante: Batteries and inverter first, then panels, then Starlink. Test each module before connecting the next one.
Check polarity before connecting: negative to negative, positive to positive. A short circuit in batteries is instant.
Set the inverter's low-voltage cutoff (11.5 V on 12 V; 40 V on 48 V) so deep discharges don't damage the batteries.
Activate Starlink and its subscription. Run a speed test; adjust the position if latency is high or packets are being lost.
Test the generator outdoors: 30 minutes under load, fuel stabilized.
despues: Clean the panels every 2–3 months: dust, fallen leaves and bird droppings cut efficiency by 20–30%.
Check connections and fuses every 6 months: corrosion, loose screws and frayed cables cause most failures.
Battery test once a month: voltage and temperature. A cell that runs hotter than the rest is going to fail.
Test the generator every 3 months (30 min under load). Don't leave petrol in the tank for more than 6 months.
Renew your Starlink plan before it expires: prices sometimes change when you reactivate.

errores: Buying panels without an inverter or batteries. Panels only generate with sun: without storage you have nothing at night. Batteries and inverter first, then panels.
Installing lead-acid batteries in 2026. LFP lithium costs 3–4× more but lasts 5× longer (3,000+ cycles vs 500–1,000): it works out cheaper per cycle.
Putting Starlink where the sky is obstructed. It needs ~100° of clear sky; trees, roofs or mountains block the signal. Roof or terrace with an open view.
Running the generator indoors. CO is invisible and odourless and kills in minutes: always outdoors, ventilated, 3+ metres from windows and doors.
Skipping a professional installation. Poorly anchored panels fly off, badly connected batteries catch fire, unprotected cables melt. €200–500 for a certified installation is worth every cent.
